Life is Strange is one of those choice-based story games that is in the same vein of Telltale games. It stands out as a top-tier title in this niche genre for its high concept story, which was met with surprisingly fluid game mechanics and a multitude of choices that have lasting consequences. Though the genre suffers with only a few choices really mattering in the grand scheme of things, Life is Strange does a terrific job of carrying changes over into other episodes with unpredictable consequences. While the mechanics allow for you to entertain the consequences of all options, you are ultimately tasked to select one before progressing. But knowing the reactions ahead of time allows for you to make a more informed decision without having to replay the entire game or episode over in full length.
As for the story, I'll just say that an ordinary teenage girl gets the power to rewind time and uses it to cope with life in a small forest-y town. Despite the cringy dialogue and out-of-date memes that accurately described adolescence years ago, the sheer mystery of character motivations will keep you going through the episodes. The writers also went to a great length to pace out the storylines - nothing ever felt rushed. If anything, you might feel that you wished that there were more opportunities to connect with minor characters. I guess that's what fanfic is for.
TL;DR - Life Is Strange is an outstanding game in the Telltale-like story rich genre for it's near-perfect triangle of mechanics meeting original storytelling that shares a good balance of gameplay with the cutscenes. You may feel a little off-put by the environment and some characters, but you'll always want to know what they're up to and what role they have to play in the story.

Upon buying the game "Mountain", it was delivered to my library immediately which suprised me positively.
As for the package for this product, I can say I am satisfied. The game was not damaged after delivery, only a tiny little scratch on the backside, but I personally do not find it disturbing as it does NOT affect gameplay in any way.
The packafe contains the game, forums and guides. Then I launched the game, not before having read through the license of agreement and notes for the safe use of this game carefully.
The intro shows all companies involved in the making of this game. Luckily, the intro can be skipped upon pressing enter, this will save a lot of time in the future.
The graphics are very good looking- thanks to the physic/graphic engine develoved just for this game. I myself disliked the strong effects at times, referring to the motion blur and lens flare, luckily it is possible to turn these effects off in the video option screen. The graphics can be ranked as "Next-gen" for sure.
I've benchmarked this game on two different machines; one AMD and one intel/nVidia run each. It is a slight better performance on the AMD machines, but that might be just me.
Unfortunately, the game did NOT support my Logitech G27 Steering wheel, so I had to stick to my Razer Deathadder 2015 Chroma and Savior gaming keyboard. This is a real bummer, looking at the fact I bought this Logitech G27 steering wheel just for the sake of enjoying "Mountain" even more.
I will not talk much about the gameplay itself since I do not want to spoil anything, however I will talk about the mechanism the game works with.
The playground is a open world, taking place on a mountain, based on surviving the difficulities of mother nature.
It features a lot of variants on how the game can be completed. Please keep in mind that there is no real way of failing, however there is no way to achieve 100% either. Due to the missing challenge at occasions I found the game not too interesting at times, however I have enjoyed the gameplay so far.
I myself think trying and finding out for yourself is the best way of knowing whether you like the game or not :)
TL;DR: The game is a very challenging game, newbies will find themself helpless at times, but luckily there are many guides to read through to help out.

First off, this game is very short in its current form. It is only the first episode which clocks in at about 3 hours of playtime. Fortunately, the second episode has already been crowd-funded and I think is coming later this year. People who have already bought the first episode will get the second for free. It is up to you to decide whether or not 3 hours of gameplay is worth 15$ or whether you'd rather buy it on sale. I'm not sure how long the second episode will be.
That said, this is a beautiful game. It's strength lies in the storytelling, voice acting, characters, and artwork. The story is very interesting and the ending is very much a cliff-hanger. The developers did a great job of pulling in the player and getting the excited for the second episode. The characters are all pretty funny, especially the hipster lumberjack who wears uggs, gets snobby about art, and has a record player. The brilliance of the story, however, lies beneath the surface. At times, it seems childish or even shallow but that is simply a part of the story itself. If you pay attention, you'll quickly notice all sorts of weird things about the game. Like,
It goes without saying that this game is filled with commentary on belief, identity, and freedom, from the odd little religious cults that Vella encounters on her quest to kill Mog Chothra to the "choice" Shay has on his space ship. All of this is complemented by a very well done cast of characters with some pretty impressive voice acting from Elijah Wood, Jack Black, Masasa Moyo, and Wil Wheaton.
The only shortcoming of the game is in the gameplay. Now, I am not a fan of point and click games, so I only play them when the story looks amazing. But even so, I noticed how easy most of the puzzles where. It never took me that long to figure out what I had to do and I never had to look up any walkthroughs. This is nothing like Machinarium for example, which forced me to resort to a walkthrough occasionally. Despite this one drawback, which hopefully they will improve on in the second episode, this game is well worth getting, even in its short, and unfinished state. If you don't want to drop 15$ for such a short game, wait for a sale. Either way, it is great game.

I'm recommending this game, but only because I'm biased. I like short, minimalist narrative games, and I like Brazilian culture, so I appreciate this game more than most people. If you don't like either of those things, this game won't change your mind.
The Last NightMary: a Lenda do Cabeça de Cuia (literally: the legend of gourd head) is a short narrative game based on folklore famous in the Northeast Region of Brazil. Cabeça de Cuia is an undead monster, and he's out to kill the protagonist, who has been hallucinating about him for some time. The goal is to avoid capture, and find a way to put him to rest.
Most of the gameplay is split between two sections, wandering a grassland maze, and light inventory puzzles. The maze is not very fun; there aren't many landmarks leading you to your destination, so its easy to get lost. There is no map screen, and if you pause to get your bearings, the monster is likely to come out of the bushes and attack you, giving you a few seconds to click to another part of the maze, or die. A map screen would have made it a lot more manageable, especially a real-time one to make it more tense with the monster chasing you.
The inventory puzzles are easy, but fine. At first the puzzles are only in places where the protagonist is safe, but there are a small number in the maze later on. Interestingly, around 90% of the "puzzles" are simply looking for objects located in places around the environment. It's not quite a hidden object game, but it's reminiscent of them. Most of the true puzzles are thankfully straightforward. Match to lamp, knife to rope, battery to radio, etc. The last puzzle was very challenging, so much that I needed some hints to solve it. It wasn't something that I thought I would figure out in my own, but there was a type of logic to it that made it less frustrating than other adventure games.
The art is very good. Many of the puzzle screens remind me of impressionist paintings, albeit morbid ones. The river in particular would make a great computer background. The way Cabeça de Cuia's previous victims are portrayed is very sad. It makes it easy to be sympathetic towards them, despite them not having any dialogue or any real interaction with you. Drowned Mary is particularly effective, I cringed when I saw what had happened to her.
The sound design is decent as well. The sound effects do a good job of building tension, especially with the monster and other sudden sounds. There is occasionally music, which isn't bad, but isn't something I found particularly memorable. There is a surprising amount of voice acting as well. It's mostly fine, but the delivery leaves a bit to be desired. I'm not fluent in Portuguese (yet), but it feels like the actress was reading from a script and not in any actual danger.
In summary, this game is actually not bad. It's a bit barebones, but shows high enough production value to be worth the price. I would for sure recommend it on a sale, and will be hoping for a new game from this developer.

The Last NightMary is a relatively simple horror game, with a little bit of replayability, particularly for achievements and alternate endings, with each runthrough talking 10-20 minutes.
To start off with the problems, firstly, the game would, even though it's short, benefit from a save function, and I found the lack of that rather frustrating, particularly as it's tough to skip through the opening text. I played the game in windowed mode, and I did also find some issues with some text, especially during the endings, being cut off. I didn't try it in full screen, so that may be a better option for gameplay. Finally, the last problem that really shows up is that the game was originally in Portuguese, and while the translation is mostly good, there's still some problems, and the endings and journal entries, in particular, really could have improved writing to flow better in English.
All that said, the game is ultimately meant to be scary, and the game goes about it in a way that is fairly straightforward, but really effective. The sound of the demon (of sorts) in the game approaching is fairly unpredictable (if not random), but it gives the game a frantic pace, and since I started playing this in the middle of the night, it did a good enough job for me to stop playing until it would be daylight.
Overall, for a few bucks it's a decent (although not great) storyline and a pretty effective scare the first few run throughs.

I found this game to be very enjoyable, although it's certainly not for everyone. Hotline Miami gets a lot of its style from the difficulty in many of the levels. Disclaimer: you will die over and over again. That said, the levels are usually quick and compact enough that dying at the end of a level doesn't always feel like the game cheated you out of a victory. But the game will sometimes cheat you. Expect enemies to occasionally run through walls, or dog A.I. to not exist at all.
Hotline Miami very unique gameplay. As you complete stages, you unlock various masks, and these give varying effects, and they are all a lot of fun to use. Some masks perform better on different stages, and it's fun to expirement and see which ones you like best.
The soundtrack is probably the best part of the game, and that's saying lots. You won't care that you're dying a thousand times every level because you'll be too busy jamming out to sweet electronic beats throughout the whole game.
The story, while not a total blockbuster, is rather interesting. I won't spoil it here, but i quite enjoyed the premise, though it was a bit confusing at times. The story may seem hard to follow at some points, but this actually helps the story because neither the character nor the player will understand the bigger picture of murdering hundreds of dudes and enjoying every minute of it.
Hotline Miami has a lot of replay value, and i found myself coming back to the same stages several times after i beat the game the first time. The masks along with a grading system encourages players to try different tactics to try and get the best score they can. There are even some bonus stages, a hidden message throughout the game, and secret achievements if you want some bonus content.
Overall, Hotline Miami is a fantastic game. With amazing soundtrack, fast-paced gameplay, and delightful graphics and replayability, it won't leave you wanting more. If you're not a big fan of the difficulty, it might not be the best purchase, but I highly reccomend Hotline Miami to anyone who really likes hurting other people.

Out of the games I have played on steam, Garry's Mod was my first, and I was not dissapointed.
Sure, it didn't make much sense at first, but once you play for a good while and explore the workshop, you will learn that you are playing with the complete power of the game, all at your hands.
Whether you like Garry's Mod or not, it was one of the few games that me and my siblings could all play together, so it still is special to me, which I hope it is to you somehow.
Gameplay
When it comes to gameplay, you can do whatever you want. You can get addons and maps in the workshop, as well as gamemodes! I can't really say much here sadly, as Garry's Mod is the most free sandbox game I have ever played. You can do whatever you want.
There are gamemodes in the workshop as I said earlier, which are probably the closest form of an actual objective-based game you can get. A few gamemodes are Trouble in Terrorist Town, Murder, Prop Hunt, and many more.
The graphics reseble Half-Life 2, which is because Garry's Mod was a mod for Half-Life 2, so it is obvious that it would look like it. I actually like this aspect though, because as long as you don't have too many addons, a potato PC can run it.
Pros
-Fun to play, especially with friends.
-Can run on a potato, as long as you don't have too many addons.
-Easy to get used too.
-Complete freedom!
-Multiple different modes to choose from.
Cons
-Still laggy for some users, but not too many.
-Not everything is in the workshop.
-You might not have any friends to play with.
Conclusion
After playing this game for over 200+ hours, I knew I needed to review it, because this game is one of the few things that my siblings and I could play on, and I think it is time to pass it on to you.

There are not so many games about ordinary people living the usual life. Life is Strange - allows us to enjoy such a rare interactive everyday life, showing it incredibly bright and lively, and then shifts focus in the direction of action and supernatural that ends on a minor note.
Experience the other life:
- Life is Strange has absorbed the best finds of the plot games of recent times, and at first it seemed that it could seriously claim the laurels of the game of the year. Everything in it is good: the gameplay and the plot were closely intertwined, the scenes were perfectly set, the soundtrack perfectly combined with the passing away youth theme, the opportunity to unwind the time back did not relieve the burden of responsibility for the decisions made, and even the episodic structure made it necessary to stop and think over the choices made (And probably discuss it with friends, but what's quite personal).
- From the very first minutes, the game bribes with utmost sincerity and attention to details: Max, our protagonist, comments on every little thing about which one can at least say something, pours a soul into a diary that allows us to deeply experience all of her emotions. The other characters were revealed through communication and other kinds of interaction with her. Max is much more like a living person than the vast majority of game protagonists in most games: she has her own circle of contacts, her tastes, and passions, her memories, and regrets, her leisure and dreams about the future.
- With regard to showing everyday stories in games, Life is Strange has set a new high standard, which should be taken as an example for both new developers and already experienced ones. However, the touching teenage drama of LiS is not limited, it contains a place for both mysticism and detective. Alas.
So what's wrong?
- The director of the game, Jean-Maxime Maurice, calls Danganronpa's dilogy among his favourite games, but there's no detective line in the detective line stretched out for a good half of Life is Strange, and there's not much of intrigue that permeates every chapter of the visual novel from Spike Chunsoft. I personally find it completely wrong because the game asks to pay attention to details as a whole and those details should be extremely valuable if it pretends to be detective oriented, it's what "Detective" genre about, and if you put it as one of the most valuable features of the game, then it has to be at least decent enough. But there're no traces of ambiguity, raisins, nothing that would justify its existence, so shouldn't have been mentioned as a game feature, since its potential kept unrevealed throughout the game.
- By the middle of the game, it almost completely replaces the magnificent interactive everyday life, which bribed from the beginning. And in the last episode, when this line comes to an end, the mystical, compelling heroine comes out to make a difficult, but still a binary choice of ending.
Your choice matters?

Pros & Cons:
Pros:
+ (Stunning work of artists, directors and sound engineers);
+ (Incredible attention to the characteristics of the characters);
+ (Warm and sincere first half of the game).
Cons:
- (The game tries to be all at once, and it does not work);
- (Useless detective line);

Result:
Aspects:	Score:
Atmosphere	10 - Strong atmosphere of a hard teen's life who faces unusual aftermath on the way.
Graphics	8.5 - There's nothing to say, it's just pleasant.
Optimization	10 - Everything is good here, no questions.
Sound	10 - Soundtrack is great, loved it so much that even spared a few weeks to learn the guitar main theme.
Animations	7.5 - Nothing special, many details as in other interactive movies.
Story	8.0 - Everything is great except for both endings. A big disappointment, unfortunately.
Gameplay	9.5 - Much more enjoyable than most of its genre, made me want to click absolutely everything I see.
Replayability	7.0 - 2 times maximum, because once you find out the story ends up poorly in 2 different ways, you probably won't ever back to the game.
Total	8.5 - Even with all the questions to the game I personally have, I still find it one of the greatest storytelling and enjoyable experience, so I strongly recommend you to lower your expectations and play it at least once.
Afterwords:
- Life is Strange is very likely to disappoint you in the final - but this isn't a reason to skip the game away. This's one of the few games in which close attention is paid not to heroism, but to ordinary people, and it is worth appreciation, even only for that.
- It's also interesting that both detective and paranormal storylines are very linear in terms of gameplay. This, on the one hand, is natural (the mystery of the disappearance of the local Laura Palmer has only one solution, and the impending tornado does not leave much room for improvisation), on the other hand, it is too close to the movie.
- Nevertheless, when Life is Strange releases the protagonist to freedom, allows you to examine and comment on every detail of the environment, talk with other characters and make a decision, it seems to be a new standard for the entire genre of interactive drama, a standard that should be used as a guide by all subsequent games, developing in this direction.

Okay so a review on the game so far.
Baring in mind I played the Tech Demo for a few hours before this game officially became released.
The graphics are really really nice, really they offer some nice features and good design.
The audio is just basic engine sounds with other crane noises etc... You cannot hear the other players vehicles etc. (Release version might be patched by now)
The controls... there is where it gets a little tricky.  The controls are awkward to get used too and even when you are, you spend most time reading back over them.  It is what I do.
The game itself has is a great one and not to be played alone.  Multiplayer with 4 friends is the best, really.
If you enjoy slow 4x4 changing to find the best possible route to an objective with too much water or mud infront of you.. You then work a way around it slow on the power in a low or high gear, then get stuck and winch out or a friend winchs you out, and then you get stuck and use a crane to frog it.
Really the game is really good fun taking a slower pace to a driving simulator.  IT IS A SIMULATOR I swear.  It is really hard to get used too and you drive slow with friends.
It is realistic water terroforming, realistic terrain deforming and realisitic placement of everything, really a well made game and not to be taken as "yeah I am great at racing games" I am great at racing games and this is not a race!
You put tooooo much power on the wheels on the terrain you will become stuck because the tires dug into the terrain causing a hole... Amazing!
Driving slow, enjoying the beautiful scenary.  Yes the game has some problems like random damage loss, random rock and getting stuck really easy, but you ignore them because it fun, driving, driving, stuck.. Winch out, driving driving, stuck, friend winchs you out, driving and reach destination... You fail to read and go respawn at garage, update your vehicle and then make the journey all over again, getting stuck, winching, driving, winching etc.. Read the mission you and a friend, you get logs for example and start to drive out but now you are top heavy with a heavier truck, you get a decent distance outside turn in mud and go FULLL POWERRRR... Then the truck tips over, your friends laugh and you smile because you enjoyed it and made a silly move... Now repeat.
Really this is a great slow moving tactical approach to driving offroad game.  Looking forwward to future content and releases!
I am happy I brought this game and happy I have so much fun, if you enjoy 4x4 then this is a great game!

Before you instantly call me a Marvel hater, please read this review in its entirety. My aim is to help other people whether to buy this game or not. I love both Marvel and DC.
REVIEW:
LEGO Avengers was a really ambitious game, but ultimately feels like a downgrade from LEGO Marvel Superheroes. At this state, I cannot, in my right mind, recommend it.
Pros:
+Gameplay is a bit refined from the previous Lego Marvel game.
+The soundtrack is nice, but is a con as well (see below)
+ Huge roster of characters to play as.
+Open world New York, Wakanda, and Asgard, also a con (see below)
Neutral:
*The Avengers Story + a few other films in the MCU (Marvel Cinematic Universe) - I know the story, so the story aspect is a bit boring, but I don't mind.
Cons:
-Overall games feels a bit lazy on the devs' part. One great example is that this game, while having the Avengers soundtrack as well, recycles Lego Marvel Superheroes soundtrack.
-Another point of this is the open world looks and feels, right off the bat, unpolished and seems to be just slapped on the game just to label it open world. This is if compared to Lego Marvel Superheroes and other previous open world lego titles.
-Now the BIG one - Performance!:
All the other Lego games I have (7 through Steam and a couple more by disc, excluding Avengers) have run perfectly well, even on default graphics, which are pretty high. No problems whatsoever. This game is horrible performance-wise, to say the least. I have it windowed, all my video settings are low, I've verified files, etc. The game still lags terribly, freezes at certain points, and I believe I've had 1-2 crashes so far. Some bugs too (such as Coulson's gun dangling from his right foot).
Such a shame, because I really wanted to enjoy this. Made me skeptical of Lego Marvel Superheroes 2.
Oh, and just as a comparison: I have around 160 hours in Lego Marvel Superheroes right now. Sad that Lego Avengers will get nowhere near as that. Maximum 10 hours is all this game deserves, if I can bear through 8 more hours of pure lag...
I'm beginning to suspect that the company that makes these Lego videogames are beginning, or have already started, to spew out a Lego game each year, not bothering about the quality of the game. Lego Marvel Superheroes 2 may just be a Make-or-Break moment for me. If it is a Break, then I guess you lost a customer, Lego Videogames!
Thank you for reading this review! I really wanted to like this game and I like it, but through clenched teeth.
Some advice for LEGO game buyers:
Great Lego Superhero games: all of the Lego Batman ones, Lego Marvel Superheroes 1 & 2
Great Lego games in general: the ones listed above, Lego Lord of the Rings, Lego Indiana Jones 1, both Lego Harry Potters.
P.S. If I need to update this review, I will. I really wish Lego will fix this game with a patch. If they don't, then they just left a broken game up on Steam, which is a huge rip-off. Please fix this game, Lego!
UPDATE (12/19/2017):
I've adjusted some (ironically) in-game settings and the game runs better. I was able to finish the story and am working on the open world. It's still laggy at times though and the computer buttons need to be pressed harder than in other Lego games. Lego Marvel Superheroes 1 and 2 are still better. Here is my ranking of the Lego Marvel games:
1. Lego Marvel Superheroes 2
2. Lego Marvel Superheroes
3. Lego Marvel Avengers
Note that Lego Avengers is mostly an experiment to transition from Lego Marvel Superheroes 1 to 2.

Super Blue Fighter is an arcade game about a blue boxer which is assigned to kill a monster with the appropriate color in each round. There are two colors which will change each round, designating which monster to kill. After you kill all of the specified enemies in the said round, you'll move to the next round, with new enemies and more hordes. You have 60 seconds in each round to kill the specified monster before you ended up with a game over. The game is endless, meaning that you have to play until you die.
There are roughly 2 bgms in the game; the main menu and in game bgm. Both bgms are a retro music, where the main menu has an encouraging vibe on it and the in game bgm has a relaxing vibe on it. I personally enjoyed both of them.
The game is using 2D sprite graphics with a simple design to reflect on its arcade genre. The UI is also designed to be retro styled, which leaves no confusion to its user.
Actually, i have described the game in the intro, so i'll explain the details here. You'll start with 3 lives and bombs and you can hold up to 5 of each items. Beside the colored enemies which you have to kill (by touching them) and the other colored enemies counterpart (which you shouldn't touch), there will be other monsters that will try to kill you. For your info, they can't be killed with touching, so you have to use either bombs or a bullet-like item which is dropped randomly in each round. If you somehow get hit by the enemies, you'll have an immunity for a few seconds if you still have at least a life left. Beside using the bomb to protect yourself, you can also slow down your time with X. However, the 60 second counter for the round completion will not be slowed down (if not going quicker).
You can kill enemies with bombs. However, the best practice is to kill a lot of enemies with one blast which will give you a super combo bonus which can give you more bombs and(or) life drops (plus a bonus score). A good strategy is to circle the non colored enemies until they gather in one spot and place the bomb in the middle of them. I didn't know about this until i played it for a few hours and i can't reach far without this trick.
Although the game is becoming harder in each round, the difficulty will not be getting harder after you have grasped the game and (or) reaching a particular level.
There are some issues with alt tabbing, however. The game will not auto paused if you alt tabbing the game and even if you pause before you alt tabbing the game, the game will automatically resumes by itself if you return to the game.
Pros:
- interesting concept
- different types of enemies with their own attacking style
- easy to learn
Cons:
- the level can be hard to be tracked because it's disappear quickly (and you also have to keep track on the color after the round change)
- the game will not auto pause when you are alt tabbing
- although you paused the game before alt tabbing, the game will auto resume when you returns to the game

As a preface, I was not a backer and knew nothing of the origin story of this game when I decided to purchase it.
Pros:
- The artwork is gorgeous
- The music is lovely
- Neat concept of telling two stories / giving the player the option to play two characters
- Imaginative story elements (love the space weaver!)
- I like the self actualization / empowerment theme
Cons:
- Based on reviews I had read, I thought this game was aimed at adults.  While charming in its own way, it is aimed, in my opinion, squarely at small children.
-  Cause and effect are not strongly correlated in this game.  While whimsical and perhaps dreamlike, this makes gameplay feel rather unrewarding.
- Storyline issues - one of the main characters has to fight for her life within the first few minutes of gameplay.  Unfortunately, this is not at all a stressful event because I 1) haven't been given enough time to really care about her, 2) no tension is built up b/c none of the other characters seems to be very concerned about her, and 3) during the actual fight scene, making a wrong choice has no negative outcome. I understand that as a point and click puzzle, you may need several tries to figure it out, and can understand why the developers made the choice to limit the negative consequences of missing the puzzle.  However, I would argue that a life or death situation requires negative consequences - otherwise, you are proving to the player that there is no real "problem" to be solved in the game - you have eliminated the biggest "problem" there can be.
-  There is no finesse needed to interact with non player characters;I found myself simply clicking through the options as quickly as possible to get on with it already.  Several times I didn't even really pay close attention to the dialogue - but this largely did not affect my ability to complete the puzzles.
- The puzzles, while at times cute / funny, were pretty inconsistent.   At times they were overly simple or simply bizarre / illogical, leading to a "click until you find it" strategy being a valid method of progressing through the game.
All in all, my critiques can be ignored if one looks at this game as aimed at children. If it is a children's game, all of these choices make sense - don't make the game too scary or too hard, put most of the emphasis on the whimsy and a positive message. So maybe I was just mislead by the reviews.

Remember the old trope of the top down 2D Japanese RPG where a dozen of sidekicks followed the movement of your main character by the letter? Well, somebody decided they could use this “movement mechanic” and drop it in the side scrolling environment, with a dash of Bit Trip Runner in it. If you also though the results of this mixup would be awesome, you are woefully mistaken: hence we got an abomination of the game called JumpBall.
Rant begins! Ever wanted to feel your eyes and soul bleeding out of the pores of your skin profusely? Than you have to play this travesty. You have four chowder heads following and copying the moves of the front doink controlled by the player, as they jump and try to avoid spikes on the road. There are only two commands in this game: press up and you do a high jump, press down and you do a small jump. That’s it, I’ve just explained the whole sheisty game. You have two modes, both battling for your attention due to incredible amount of crap they’re stuffed with: Tower mode and road mode. Tower mode is made out of vertical platforms where spikes are moving left and right and you try to jump and avoid them in hope that you’ll reach the last platform. In road mode, you have a set of horizontal levels of increasing difficulty, where you and your crew of boneheads try to reach the right side of the screen and the end of the level, while avoiding raised platforms, spikes and other nonsense that will gladly and unfairly try to reset your progress, with each level taking no more than 15-30 seconds if you don’t screw it up. And if you thought that you’ve got the “skills”, you’ll soon reach level five or six, where the difficulty will spike out so incredibly high, you’ll stay permanently stuck in this digital hell hole, repeating like a drone your moves in hope that next time you’ll finish the level, while the music made out of ONE annoying track will keep incessantly rebooting until your ears dry out and your brain fails to compute. And if that’s not enough salt to put on the injury, the background graphics are the single most hideous, nausea inducing, eye hemorrhaging attack on all the senses I’ve ever witnessed. As you move and the background made out of different, repetitious geometrical designs with tacky and blinding set of colors moves as well, you will feel physically sick and psychologically scarred.
If you’ll pardon my French, but eff this game, and if you value your sanity and wellbeing, you’ll stay away from this lost cause. I give it a fritter away out of Codswallop. Just play Bit Trip Runner instead... or any other game for that matter. Rant over!

This game caught me by surprise when I got it in a bundle a few months ago. I hadn't played it for a while because I didn't have time to invest in starting a new game. A couple weeks back, however, I was browsing around my Steam library, looking for something I could play in short sessions, and I started Nuclear Throne (using an XBOne controller).
Of course, I got killed almost immediately in the Desert at the first burst of bullets from a spider, and of course, I didn't admit defeat and jumped right back in as Crystal, and I got killed even faster, but the patterns started showing up. Next thing I knew, I was obsessed with getting as far as I could on this game.
The next few days, I invited a friend over to try out the game in co-op, and it quickly became a struggle of not dying and reviving each other, getting better with each run, but with the eventual Desert deaths in between.
40hrs total into the game, Nuclear Throne has become an obsession among my circle of friends, and we get together at every chance we get to see how far we can get and to find all of this game's secrets.

Let me start out by saying this isn't my normal type of game. I've only played a few visual novels, avoided Gone Home like the plague, I never watch shows with high schoolers, etc. But when I found out the first episode was free I thought I'd give it a shot, and was shocked by how much I enjoyed it. I'm not telling you this for "gamer cred" or whatever, but to explain that the fact that I actually liked this game despite hating the genre it's in is a testament to its quality.
The amount of things that you can observe and/or interact with is pretty impressive. Thankfully, the voice acting is pretty good, considering Max has something to say about every little thing you look at. Sadly, this quality voice acting is somewhat ruined by weak facial animations, which make the characters look like animatronics.
The choices are also much better than I expected. I came into this game thinking the choices would be the Fallout 3-style "kick a puppy or don't" moral choices where the right answer is obvious, but each choice is in a pretty gray area, where you have to juggle helping others while also saving your own hide. Of course, part of what makes the choices so interesting is Max's ability to reverse time, allowing you to see the immediate outcome of each choice.
This is ability also helps you solve puzzles, and is probably one of the reasons I liked this game over other story-based games.
Like the choices, many of the characters are in a gray area. In the intro they seem to fit into one-dimensional stereotypes, but as you play the game you'll find that maybe the bully is covering up insecurities, etc.
My biggest complaint is that the game felt too sectioned. I'm not demanding a big open world, but it would have been nice to explore the entire Blackwell campus, for example, instead of only the main campus, then only the dorms, etc., only moving to areas that are directly related to the story.
Overall, since the first episode is free, you should at least check it out.
/10
UPDATE: Some of the choices are pretty soul-crushing, so if you need something to cheer you up you should look elsewhere.

There are millions and millions of reviews about this game, all saying the same thing. This game will hit you in the feels and stay with you long after you have finished it. Even in between episodes, when the hastily taped up snow globe of my emotions was put on the shelf to rest, to recuperate, to strain against the cracks; I felt the characters, the story, the things I had yet to find out and understand, lurking in the shadows of my mind!
This game does a good job at making you care about the characters, even those that are less pleasant, you want to try and help where you can. Surely there is reason for their depression or outward meanness?! This is where being nosy helps! Admittedly, I probably would not get away with Max's level of blatant snooping, like say, going through laptops and tablets right in front of said owners, or looting through rubbish bins! But the tidbits of information picked up and mental commentary helped to flesh out the world and environment. So much so, that I actually felt like I had been a student at Blackwell Academy and lived in Arcadia Bay after a while!
Do not read up anything about this game before you play! Even the inkling about a character or their motivations will ruin it for you! Going in blind is always best, and will have the most impact as the story unfurls about you.
The soundtrack! The soothing indie vibes that describe, only too well, the pains of growing up and those confusing teenage years. The lush almost water-coloured backdrop of Arcadia Bay. First off... I play many types of games but one type I usually sway away from is car games. Besides the gta series and Need for Speed: Underground (which I enjoyed mostly because I like to pimp out my car) I never played too many. Then there is this game...Spintires.
Right off the bat going into this game I can allready notice the amount of detail put into the environments and the vehicles. The paint of the all of the trucks looks realistic and the gitty feeling of seeing your muddy truck dive into a river and emerge from the other side muck free is great eye candy which never gets old.
Next is the ability to play with others in cooperative play. My first foray into this game was multiplayer and it went something like this... We all eagerly jump into the first truck and fly straight into the road ahead of us and within 15 seconds each of us are stuck. So one of us finds out how to switch trucks and proceeds to try and wench each of the stuck noobs back to safety. As the night went on we got better at controlling the beasts of burden and started completing some of the objectives.
As of now in game the only real goals are...
1. Deliver lumber to different locations on the map.
2. Clear the map of "cloaks" which obstruct your map.
3. Unlock other garages by delivering garage points using special add-ons on the trucks.
4. Finding some of the hidden trucks that aren't available from the starting spawn garage.
Also if you like to unlock achievements then there are plenty to strive for and the game will have you trekking through miles of dirt, mud, and rocks to get them all.
There are a few minor bugs like a chat bug where players swap names and the saving in my opinion needs to be reworked... as of now you cannot reload multiplayer games so if you intend to try and beat a map with friends... make sure you have plenty of time to play. But all these bugs are outside of the driving aspect of the game so I really can't complain.
Finally, I can see myself playing for a long time to come and even at the moderately steep price I can fully back this game. Its challenging, pretty, and I haven't played anything like it.
Buy it. :)

Hi everyone, I tried both demos (2011 and 2013) because I'm the type of player who likes simulation when it comes to racing and such, and also because I like physics based simulations as well.
As you may know Havok (at least for me and for others) is one of the best physics engine in the market and it can deliver both performance and incredible level of detail when it comes to those little things or important ones as in this case terrain/tyre/chassis/body deformation, damage (both visual and mechanical failures), water and dust interacting with objects in real time, day/night cycles, and all of this in a fully explorable sandbox game made by the Oovee guys.
If you enjoy all of that, have in mind that this game is based with OFF ROAD in mind, which includes an amazing landscape with different type of landscapes, surfaces like mud and such with real interaction depending in the weight of the vehicle, the type of tyres you equiped and so on.
Add to the list the amount and type of cars/trucks/jeeps/tanks/buggy´s...etc, all of them with modifications so you can interact even more with the environment and to complete objectives that you can find in the world.
Don't forget this game comes with the idea of MODS so you can create or download others people creations and make it even better or just play with the vehicles you really want.
Do you want to make a "Camel Trophy" type of "race" with your friends? You can thanks to the 4 player online mode in where you can choose the map if you are the host or vote for the map you all want.
You can explore and try different things/ways, you can race but in a different way setting objectives if you want and then try to get to the point faster than the other players, you can assist your friends with a hook or crane if they get stuck in the mud like happens in real life, etc.
I mean you enjoy what you do and it feels authentic.

If you want a SP experience only you have an objective based SP mode in where you need to complete objectives by discovering the map, and in the way you are going to unlock new vehicles and features for them (different type of tyres/cranes/repair kits, etc).
If you like a low paced but quite entertained experience this is the game for you. Get dirty...then wash it on the river...you can do it. ;)

> Subscribe to the Paladins YouTube Channel (and PaladinsVOD) so you can watch their eSports Tournaments every now and then
> Don't sweat accumulating Gold/Crystals - If you spend 30 seconds logging in daily you'll get more than enough in no time (well - not MORE than enough, but enough for it to stay fun and not become grindy)
Also:
The Devs are super hands on, they change stuff constantly but are in touch with the community at all times and genuinely care about listening to us and go to great lengths to make a game that we can all enjoy.
Possibly the best thing about the 3 months I have spent with this game so far, is watching it evolve.

Super Blue Fighter is Herrero Games’ return to Steam following its positively reviewed Job the Leprechaun that was released in August, 2015. Where Job is a well designed casual platformer this time around the developers have opted to develop a simplistic arcade survival game. The object of the game is to hit the right color of the robots to get the maximum score and avoiding the many enemies on the field. The robots that you are to hit are demonstrated by the color of the stars in the background. When they are green you hit the green robots and when they are red you target the red ones. There are a number of different enemy types including the robots of the color that you’re not supposed to hit and the further you advance into the game the more varied enemy types will show up and attempt to kill you.
Super Blue Fighter was an easy selection for a new entrant on my Steam library’s favorites list. That is just how much I enjoyed this one. It is a game that I know that I’ll return to again and again when I have short periods to play games beyond the scope of this website to enjoy games for my own personal gain without any other thought.

Super Blue Fighter is an arcade, retro-style, fast-paced, 2D arena style. I believe that is the ebst description I can make of this game. Let's review the main points of this game:

+ The gameplay is smooth and the mechanics are fairly simple to understand and execute.
+ The difficult curve ramps up really well, each level being faster and more populated with threats.
And here are some takeaways:
- It gets boring after a while, needs more gamemodes or challenges in order to keep it interesting.
- The game menus are surprisingly bad in contrast to the really good gameplay:
- Can't select resolution, windowed mode... No graphical options at all.
- Can't rebind controls, which in my particular case, is really annoying, since I usually tend to use WASD for movement        and not the arrow keys.
My final judgement is that this game has huge potential and room for many upgrades. However, I also must admit that it plays really nice and it's really entertaining for what it is currently offering.

I was rather worried about all the bad reviews, and the awful metascore this game had recieved, but given my interest in games like Killing Floor and Halo, I figured I'd give it a shot. I mean, how bad can dinosaur killing be, right?
I downloaded the free trial, and WOW was I in for a surprise. It was just good, clean fun. It didn't feel as tight as Killing Floor, or as "Next-Gen" as Halo usually does, but the combination of those two, and lack of real seriousness about the game make a fantastically fun time sink, and an extremely enjoyable game.
Within 15 minutes, I decided it was worth the $0.99 to pick this game up, as I had already had more fun playing it than I have had in a game like this since Killing Floor, and I do not regret it one bit, especially at this price.
While there are a few bugs here and there, such as dinos occasionally flying up to unbelievable heights, and arrows hovering after they have fired and hit a target. But there doesn't seem to be much of anything that gets in the way of the actual gameplay.
While to this point, I have not strayed much from the Players vs. Dinosaurs Survival mode (which is truly fantastic when you get a good group of people playing with you), there are many other different gameplay modes that provide good variety. Also, there is a pretty good selection of weapons in this game, catering to many different tastes, and nothing seems to be TOO over powered, with weapons seeming to be rather well balanced. The different "Augmentations" are also a nice addition to the game, allowing you to play to your own strengths instead of always having a vanilla character.
TL;DR:
Overall, this is a really good game, and has changed a lot for the better from the game that recieved a 35 metascore. Definitely worth the $1 it is right now, and probably even the $10 or $15 it is at full price.

Super Blue Fighter is a fun to play casual indie game with arcade characteristics. This game is an excellent entertainer in terms that it removes boredom and is for all ages. It can also serve its purpose to the more intune gamers, as a fun retro fps game.
In this game your task as a player is to touch all the system selected units, without crossing over to the wrong colored units. You do this on a square grid, be aware the purpose of this game is only to entertain. So theres not much of a storyline, but there is however a leader board where your scores get recorded. You can just touch your system specific colored unit and gain points. You can even do this by planting bombs.
But be careful of this addicting game, it can take hours of your play time with its simple design, presentability and concept.Some times you get shot by other units and die, or get trapped by your own bombs and in that way it is fun gameplay. The music is good, but the graphics is early 80's.
There are many pros and no cons to this game, but to mention a few:-
PROS
1. Its simple yet addicting
2. It has got neat music
3. It cuts out boredom
4. Its pocket friendly
CONS
1.The only draw back is it has got no story line

Wow, I just finished Act 1 in Broken Age, and it was awesome! Fascinating story, insane twists, some good humour, interesting puzzles, this is a great point-and-click game! I don't often go for point-and-click, I'm more of a survival horror or realistic FPS gamer, however I'm very glad that I bought this. The artwork, the soundtrack, the voice acting (I swear one of the characters sound like Jack Black!), and the world that is portrayed is very unique. I sadly only got 4 hours out of the playthrough (Yeah, Angry Joe wouldn't approve...), but it was 4 hours of quality. If Act 2 is included in this purchase, I'd definitely say it's worth the price, however if Act 2 is a whole seperate game that costs more than $15, I might think twice.
Yeah it's awesome, but I don't think there's much replay value here. I guess it all depends, if you like interesting characters, stories, worlds, twists, all in an artistic point-and-click game that will more than likely have some sequels, yet can overlook a somewhat lack of replayability and a less than 5 hour playthrough, then this is definitely for you. I typically consider myself a strictly FPS/RPG/Survival Horror gamer, yet this caught my attention and I'm glad I played it, so I suggest giving it a look to see if it tickles your fancy. Shooty-bang-s'plody-wow is good fun, but so is sitting down with an easy going story-driven point-and-click as well :)

The Last NightMary, developed by Submersivo Game Studio, doesn’t bring anything groundbreaking to the point-and-click genera, but it makes up for this with its narrative and intrigue.
Most of the player’s time is spent wandering through misty marshlands, hunting for different clue items scattered throughout the maze. Oddly, despite looking quite nice, the maze’s layout isn’t very distinct, which resulted in me walking in a circle five times before getting anywhere.  But the satisfaction I felt when stumbling across a rotten fishing dock, or the aging ruins of a forsaken hut, made up for it.
The puzzles are nothing to write home about. They don’t break from the norm, but they get the job done. Sometimes quantity surpasses quality. They’re simple, fun and they don’t hold your hand.
The monster, again, is nothing special. He will occasionally present himself in random areas of the maze, sometimes through a guttural cry of agony, or a sudden leap from the tall grass. He isn’t too scary, per say, but knowing that he may appear at any moment forced me into an uneasy haste.
I managed to beat The Last Nightmary in a little under an hour, BUT there is still a large majority of content I haven’t discovered yet. In fact, the game itself encourages players to run through it multiple times. I ended up with the ‘GOOD’ ending, but I’m definitely gonna give the game a few more tries.
Lastly, the English translation isn’t the best. Anyone who’s grasped the language will spot a fair amount of mistranslations in the game’s text. But, seeing as this was developed by a group of college kids from Brazil, I’m still satisfied with the outcome.
To sum it all up, The Last Nightmary is a fun, simple horror experience that should keep you interested from beginning to end. I assume you can soak up 3 to 4 hours of this game if you attempt to unlock all the endings and secrets. For its asking price, I’d say it’s worth a buy.

This game is amazing, now let me tell you why. It sounds like a simple game, drive large (and some small) foreign trucks around a mud-filled map and pick up and deliver logs. Sounds easy? You'll find doing these tasks is actually rather challenging. The maps are designed around uncovering and planning the best route to take in order to get the job done. Sometimes you'll be faced with crossing huge rivers, rock filled mudpits, other times you'll be treated to plain old ashphalt.
Strategizing and planning is part of the fun, and the rest comes from the amazingly trim and well optimized engine. The game, at release, is a whopping 595MB!  The particle, smoke and terrain deformation effects are all very well done and are a treat to look at. The maps are gorgeous, you will find yourself immediatley immersed in them. The sounds of rushing river water, chirping birds, crackling trees as you plow through them all add to make this game as realistic as possible.
The camera takes getting used to as it does control differently than anything else I have ever used. Once you do learn how it works, you'll find it irreplaceable. No need for 1st person cameras here. This is not a game of speed, but a game of strategy. You need to be able to see all sides of your vehicle, sometimes all at once in order to make it through trecherous terrain. I have read that the developers are thinking about adding in a cockpit view camera. I can almost assure you I will not use it. It would have almost no function in this game, and once you play, you will see what I mean.
This game has been a while in the making and I am glad its finally here. Planned future mod support and DLC from the developers will give this game a long life. I, for one will be there along the way.

No mindexplosion here
Wasteland 1 was a revolution. Games on the C64 were simple. Some of those guys and girls created The Bard's Tale and The Bard's Tale 3. They were my childhood heros and a big influence. Bard's Tale series were also quite simple but also quite addicting. Simple 21x21 dungeons with riddles and traps.
Then Wasteland 1. Characters had skills. A major step forward. Instead of "You see enemies at 30" would you like to (F)ight (A)dvance or (R)un" you actually saw the enemies. People from your group could break out of formation and move towards the enemy while the rest remained stationary.
But what really was special about Wasteland 1 was that there were areas you couldn't enter at the beginning and all you had were mechanical and brawling weapons. And you slowly progressed, solving riddles, making your way. There was one town that didn't allow you to enter and after many hours you finally got ahold of some energy weapons. Yeah baby! And you returned and blasted those arrogant ♥♥♥♥ guards' heads off, looting their armor and weapons and ammo. Then you progressed inside the town to try and solve the riddle, the mystery. Mind blown, truly.
Now Wasteland 2.
First of all. It's a generic, linear and tier based game with a main storyline and sidequests, all nicely placed in your journal. The first quest after the starting zone quest might seems like it gives you choice but that's just an illusion. It doesn't matter which one you pick. You'll have to go through certain main storyline areas regardless. A game on wheels.
There is no skill tree. The tree is a list. And you have stuff like Toaster repair. One would imagine that after a nuclear war toaster repair would be the least needed "skill". Something like camp building, scavanging, weapon repair or armor repair or digging or climing sounds more like it would be something that would be needed after a nuclear holocaust. There's nothing like this. It reeks of simplification and consolitis. A game for the WoW generation.
The graphics.... boxes. Everywhere. Characters look like they're straight from Everquest 1. Basic low-poly models. It's ugly. Buildings are boxes. There is no art. It's just boxes. Zones are designed like "hey let's place this box here and that box there" "and place a safe here and another container there". Everything looks the same. Bunch of boxes.
The humor... well some might find it funny that some guys dressed in black and nuns carry ♥♥♥♥♥♥ around. Anything remotely philosophical doesn't exist in this game. It's like watching explosions on TV all day. Just that there are no explosions. The story is flat and uninteresting. The humor is like "look someone said♥♥♥♥♥♥♥teeheeheee" aimed at 12 year olds.
Progression, as said, is linear and tier-based. Every weapon has an upgrade. This one does 5-12 damage, next one does 8-16 damage. The "weaponsmith" skill lets you disassemble weapons for mods or junk parts. Both can be sold, mods can be applied. Since your inventory is always more or less full you have to pick the weaponsmith skill so your're able to make some money to buy ammo. The majority of the game you'll be managing your inventory, trying to open containers and running around. Zones are made intentionally that you have to spend quite a while running around so you have the impression of huge zones. Worst example is the railway station map. If this game has 60 hours of play time 30 are spent on walking around.
Wasteland 1 was an innovator. Wasteland 2 brings nothing new on the table. We've seen this before in other games and better. It promised that my mind would explode like a blood sausage. No it didn't. Nothing mind-blowing to see here apart from the bland, uninspired game. And only because the games of the last 10 years were mostly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ console ports doesn't excuse the game to be released in this state.
Voice-overs? Few. Most dialogues aren't voiced. Only "important" NPC ones and only the first 1 or 2 paragraphs. This game is unfinished. There are game-stopping bugs. For instance you're asked to leave a party member of yours as a hostage until you solve a quest. You solve the quest and when the part member is about to return to your party instead you get a message that your party is full. You can't hire new members since the size of your party magically shrunk to 7 instead of 8. But you still have to carry around all its gear and ridiculously heavy quest items you can't dispose of because they're quest items. So inventory management got even more annoying.
Man this game sucks. And if you voice your opinion on their forums you get banned for it.

Take this review with a grain of salt. If there was an option in between 'Yes' and 'No', that's what I would have chosen. Also bear in mind, at the time of writing this, I have *not* completed the game. I'm not sure I'm going to just yet until they do some serious work on it. I'm about halfway through the main story. With that said, here goes... (warning: minor spoilers throughout)
-----------------------
Conclusion: 6/10 - The game feels like a beta. I'm glad it was released, but it needs some serious work. I'd hold out on buying for patches/mods. If you are really looking for something to play, the game is fun, it just lacks a large amount of polish that is necessary to make this game go from "okay" to "fantastic". Also, I hit the word limit. Definitely missed some things.
-----------------------
The Good
+ Storyline is interesting and easy to get caught up in.
+ Voice acting is great. Not everything is voice acted, but where it is, it's done well.
+ Character Customization is great. You can create your party of 4 from scratch, or use pre-made characters if you so choose. There is a large amount of build variety. However: [See associated con.]
+ Random skill-use events. While venturing out into the Wasteland, you'll often come across various obstacles that can be passed by one of your party member skills. Ie. "My wife is sick! Please help her and I'll let you loot this stash I left in my house!", in this case, a party member with the 'Field Medic' or 'Surgeon' skill would be able to heal his wife and get access to some loot.
+ Recruitable party members! From your starting party of 4, you can have up to I believe 3 more members of your party that are recruitable as you progress through the story. The first of which is available almost immediately when starting the game. These guys can help fill a lot of the gaps in your skill selection and provide some alleviation on skill-events and some flexibility in combat.
+ The game is huge. A lot of content and a lot of story. Developers suggest it'll take 60-70 hours to beat. That is awesome.
+ Random radio chatter. I really enjoyed this aspect of the game. You'll be wandering around and randomly hear radio chatter about other rangers in another part of the world checking in about taking down this fugitive or saving this town, etc... There is also random radio chatter from radio stations in major towns, from psychopaths from various factions, etc... Awesome addition to the game.
The Bad
- WEAPON JAMMING. This is absolutely my biggest complaint. I'll get weapons with a 1 or 2% chance to jam, yet they jam almost every-other encounter and cost almost an entire turn's worth of AP to unjam. Absolutely infuriating. This also goes for hit chances & skill succeed chances.
- Weapon variation. Weapon variation in this game is pretty obnoxious. I've been using a crowbar on my melee toon since about 30min into the game and I've yet to find anything better. Going through Arizona, you find the same weapons over and over again. Even at the vendors! Protip: Make sure you level weaponsmithing on one of your toons! Or you'll find yourself making the long trek to a vendor more often than you'd like.
- The travel system. The travel system in WL2 is just plain bad. I understand what the intent was, but it largely just made the experience frustrting. Areas are very large and in order to travel to the world-map, you need to find an exit on the map to "The Wasteland". Once in the wasteland, you have to travel across the map to your destination, regardless if you've visited it before or not. It's slow, tedious, and takes away from the immersion. I constantly find myself needing to travel to some distant point on the world map and thinking "Eh... Maybe I'll take a break and go play something else for a bit."
- Character customization limits. If you create your custom party when you first try out this game, chances are, you'll miss a skill that limits things your party can do. There are skills associated with opening different kinds of safes, accessing a large amount of loot, getting through various doors, remaining undetected in hostile areas, you name it. There are also quest elements requiring you have specific skills. These skills are not necessary to have, but not having them when you find a vendor that will only sell to you if you can use x skill to help him out, is upsetting to say the least. Especially to those, like myself, who enjoy doing *everything*.  [See associated pro] ALSO, be sure to level perception on at least one character. If you don't, you'll end up with your whole party perma-dying due to land-mines.
- Factions and choices are very opaque. Early on in the game you visit an area where you are assisting in getting their water system & power fixed. Afterwards, you are supposed to back a certain candidate for mayor since the previous mayor had been killed during a raider attack which you helped stop. After fixing the power/water, you exit the tunnels to find the election already underway and the "bad" candidate being elected by a landslide without you being able to do anything about it. You are treated like scum by the town & going back to your HQ everyone makes smartass comments about what a "great job" you did. Turns out, you had to do ALL of the sidequests *before* the main quests in that area, as well as a couple other arbitrary things. I was fairly frustred with this, especially seeing as how the "good" candidate was extremely happy with me for helping her out, then after the election, I was suddenly dirt. The questlines here were not very well articulated.
- Assocated with the previous con, choices are fairly hard to differentiate. You may decide you want to go for a "good guy" playthrough as you may have done in similar games. Good luck keeping that up. There's one point where you have 3 different factions all approaching you and all giving you quests to screw the others. You have no idea which one gives decent rewards, no idea which one is actually the good guy. No idea which one you should be following so you don't get in trouble with Ranger HQ. So, you guess, you end up screwing them ALL over because of this or that reason that you were unable to control. It all gets very unorganized and tedious.
- Random items you pick up that you aren't sure if you should hold onto or sell. No descriptions, just random. Protip: Hold onto ANYTHING white. Safe to sell gray stuff except for one type of item that you'll find out about shortly into the story.
The Maybe
+/- The combat system I'd say is a maybe. I personally enjoyed it, but there are a few things that made it incredibly frustrating.
+/- The grahpics aren't great. This isn't a complaint for me, but I am aware that this is a big thing for many people. This will likely be improved with future mods.
+/- Honey badgers. Honey badgers everywhere. You encounter honey badgers so often in this game, it should be renamed to "Wasteland 2: Revenge of the Honey Badger". While this isn't necessarily a bad thing, it breaks immersion for me. You look at the combat log and it's *filled* with stupid honey badger jokes and references that just repeat themselves over and over again for the duration of the encounter. Upon looting the corpses, you get a bunch of junk including "badger's nutsack". While this was humorous as first, the honey badgers quickly got old for me.
+/- Upon leveling up you are required to call into central command for a "field promotion" before being able to allocate your gained skill/attribute points. While this isn't a huge deal, it gets fairly annoying after awhile. Especially with your party all leveling at different rates. You'll end up with 2 party members having leveled, calling in, then 10 minutes later another party member, then 10 minutes later, your remaining party members. I often find myself holding out until my entire party is ready to level before calling in. Not a bad thing, just a minor annoyance.

Wasteland 2 is an old school computer role playing game like they used to make them in the 90s. With an isometric camera view, turn based combat, tons of skills and attributes to play with and of course the almighty dice roll deciding if you will make that 92% chance to hit shot or if it fails and might even hit a squad member in the back.
That is right, the game is party based. You control a core party of 4 that will have to face the challenges the wasteland throws at them together as in the original Wasteland or in Icewind Dale.
I'd recommended to pick premade characters for the first playthrough, so you have a balanced squad with enough combat and support skills to get through the game. Picking the wrong skills is something that can happen if you decide to make all characters yourself.
There is also the possibility for your characters to die, permanently.
When a party member dies you can recruit a new, unexperienced member of the desert rangers at the HQ. You can also take along NPCs you meet on your mission to spread Ranger law and order in the wasteland which expands the total size of your squad up to seven characters.
The game is often compared to Fallout and while it does have some similarities, it doesn't share the 50s retro future theme or its one player character style of gameplay. Fallout was a spiritual sequel to Wasteland. Wasteland 2 is a sequel to Wasteland, not Fallout. It has even less in common with the new spin the series has taken since the IP was bought by Bethesda.
Wasteland 2 is old school in more ways than just graphics and combat, it offers tons of dialogue, good writing, memorable factions, characters and choices that shape the Wasteland and its inhabitants.
Oh and the german translation isn't any good so far. The game might be patched later on, but I can't recommend playing it in german.

So I'm an avid FSX user since its launch in 2006. I've clocked over 1000 hours in the game, half on Vatsim/Multiplayer, other half offline. The game was tremendously helpful in my pursuit of my private pilot's license. I've been wanting a modernized flight simulator that runs on a modern OS since Windows 8 came out. I've heard of Prepar3d but I do not like its EULA policy even though I'm an undergraduate student and I'm qualified for its academic license. The interface and software for Lockheed's variant is tailored for flight training institutions and for professional environments and it's not very user friendly for the home user. I thought about converting to X-Plane but couldn't commit because I already have so many add-ons for FSX. Fast forward to 2014 and Windows 10, FSX was released on Steam (which by the way I couldn't believe, but very happy) from Dovetail and after downloading and installing the game, it was compatible 100% with Windows 10, no tweaking needed. Not only that but Dovetail made several improvements to the game even after Microsoft released Service Pack 2/Acceleration for FSX in 2007, a big one being adding their own multiplayer since GameSpy servers were shut down, major optimization for framerate issues and so on. PMDG and 90% of my addons work well with the Steam Edition and the other 10% have updates that make it compatible as well. Overall it’s a good competition to other Flight Simulators already out there and I can’t wait until Dovetail announces their new plans for 2016.

you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

This game is short, but so sweet that I'm glad there's to be an Act 2 some time later this year, or so I've heard (About the later this year thing, not about the act 2, that's been confirmed).
I've seen some reviews that list this as a game they wouldn't recommend, and I think in some cases that may be because the game can be considered a bit too linear. Choosing different dialogue options won't throw you in a different direction like in some games, and for the most part you can figure out where you need to go and what you need to do next by exhausting every line of dialogue available to you. Before I bought the game, when I saw that there were different dialogue options available to the player, I wouldn't have thought that would be the case, but it didn't bother me, per se, and here's why.
The game is beautifully rendered and a joy to look at, it has an air of whimsy and a tongue in cheek flavor that I couldn't get over. There were some jokes that would go right over kids' heads, which is probably for the best, but which didn't fail to get a laugh out of me.  You know, those kind of jokes. I always count those as a plus.
Also, despite thinking a few times that I had the game pinned down, in other words thinking that I knew where it was going, I found with good humor that I was wrong. It managed to provide a twist that I didn't see coming, and for that I have to give it some more points.
I finished the game in a few hours and I wish I had part 2 right now. I picked it up for 40 percent off (14.99) and I would say that it's worth more than that, counting the fact that there's more on the way and that I'm a sucker for a good story/twist.

This game is amazing, now let me tell you why. It sounds like a simple game, drive large (and some small) foreign trucks around a mud-filled map and pick up and deliver logs. Sounds easy? You'll find doing these tasks is actually rather challenging. The maps are designed around uncovering and planning the best route to take in order to get the job done. Sometimes you'll be faced with crossing huge rivers, rock filled mudpits, other times you'll be treated to plain old ashphalt.
Strategizing and planning is part of the fun, and the rest comes from the amazingly trim and well optimized engine. The game, at release, is a whopping 595MB!  The particle, smoke and terrain deformation effects are all very well done and are a treat to look at. The maps are gorgeous, you will find yourself immediatley immersed in them. The sounds of rushing river water, chirping birds, crackling trees as you plow through them all add to make this game as realistic as possible.
The camera takes getting used to as it does control differently than anything else I have ever used. Once you do learn how it works, you'll find it irreplaceable. No need for 1st person cameras here. This is not a game of speed, but a game of strategy. You need to be able to see all sides of your vehicle, sometimes all at once in order to make it through trecherous terrain. I have read that the developers are thinking about adding in a cockpit view camera. I can almost assure you I will not use it. It would have almost no function in this game, and once you play, you will see what I mean.
This game has been a while in the making and I am glad its finally here. Planned future mod support and DLC from the developers will give this game a long life. I, for one will be there along the way.
