To put it bluntly, Broken Age is fantastic.
The game is a classic point-and-click adventure, in the vein of the Lucasfilm Classics. For those of you who have been living under a rock for two years, Broken Age (previously known as Double Fine Adventure) was a huge kickstarter success, finishing up with over 3 million in crowd-sourced funds. Being one of the original big Kickstarter projects, there was some worry, but Double Fine pulled through in the most stylish way possible.
The game is split into two parts, which is.... split into another two parts.
This is a review of Act 1. Act 2 will be released some time this year, and here's hoping it's as good as this act. In each act there are two tales to play, both incredibly different, but linked in many, many ways. In one, you play as Vella, a girl forced into tradition. In the other you play as Shay, a boy forced to stay in a spaceship his whole life. Both stories are incredibly fun to play.
On your first playthrough you may not notice the similarities between the stories, but if you think about them and put the events together in your mind, you realise how linked these tales are. I can't describe the amazing feeling I had when I discovered these connections. I can't really describe them without completely spoiling the game though.
The gameplay is what you would expect from any adventure game. It's fun, puzzling and satisfying. The only downfall is the sheer simplicity of the puzzles. I only really got stuck on one puzzle and even then it's because I just didn't notice one item amongst the background. However, this is actually a pro for younger gamers, as they will enjoy it without getting frustrated.
The art. Oh man, the art. It's gorgeous. I can say no more, just look at the screenshots.
The music is fantastic as in most Double Fine games. Some great peaceful, ambient tunes to relax you as the gears in your head grind.
The story is obviously great, with some excellent writing. The biggest caveat in adventure games for me is feeling bored as lines and lines of text go on and on. In this game though, I was always interested, clicking on every dialogue option available. The AAA voice acting helps a lot too. Before you ask, yes, Jennifer Hale is in it.
Overall, Broken Age is a must-buy. Generally I don't preorder or buy games at launch, I just wait for a sale. But this time I did and it was worth every dollar. The length may be an issue, but for me just Act 1 was worth the purchase, but with another act on the way, there's really no reason not to buy this ASAP.
What more can I say? Brilliant art, music, puzzle design, writing, voice acting.... It all helps to make this a great, great game. Do yourself a favour and pick this up. You won't regret it.

Full Video Review =
Wasteland 2's story places you in the boots of four raw recruits to the desert rangers. The game starts you in the desert wastes of Arizona as you attend the funeral of Ace, a desert ranger who was recently killed. As the funeral ends the desert rangers leader General Vargas throws you into the deep end and sends you off to track down Ace's killer.
Let's start with character creation, in the game you start with four characters. You have the option of either creating your own characters or choose from pre existing builds, you can even have a combination of both. In terms of aesthetics the character models are not pleasant to look like and there isn't a large variety of faces to choose from. That being said the statistical side makes the appearance’s short comings up in spades. Your characters have both attributes which are things like strength and skills. There is a large range of skills available including things like lockpicking, safecracking and more. It's often best to create a diverse group after all the more skills your party has collectively, the more options you'll have throughout the game. I myself opted first for a assault rife bearing squad leader, a sniper with lockpicking and computer skills, a melee focused demolitions expert and a shotgun wielding medic, aptly named Doc.
When your not actually in a location, you'll be traversing the wastes on the world map. There are lots of locations to discover in the world and you can find hidden cache's of loot so its worth spending time to explore. On the world map you have to take several factors in to account when travelling. First is your water supply, your group has water canteens, each mile you travel will use up water and if you run out your party will take damage from dehydration. You can however stop of at any oasis you find in your travels to fill your canteens. Another factor is radiation, after all nukes do tend to leave some nasty after effects in the environment. Safe travel through irratiated zones can only be done by having the appropriate radiation suits, if you don't your party will die of radiation sickness very quickly. The world map also has random encounters not all of which are combat focused. Many will be raiders or animals that you must combat or run away from. Some will be travelling merchants or on the occasion something much more interesting.
Graphically Wasteland 2 isn't the prettiest of spectacles, However its art direction does bring a certain harsh, grittiness to the affair which is very appropriate for the post apocalyptic setting. I think the character models could have been done better as some of the models and animations have a blocky look to them which looks out of place. While it is not the prettiest of games, the effect animations such as explosions look well done. On top of that the things like NPC character art is fantastically done. On thing that does shine in the game is sound which is no surprise when
Mark Morgan who was responsible for the soundtracks to fallout and fallout 2 is your composer. Everything from music, sound effects and surprisingly voice acting is done superbly and brings a real atmosphere to the whole affair.
Let's move on to one of, if not the main part of the game, combat, after all theres plenty of dangers lurking in the wasteland and you can't avoid all of them. Those familiar with the recent X-com or the even more recent Divinity Original Sin will be right at home with Wasteland 2's tactical turn based system. Combat is straight forward and works from an action point system. Your characters attributes determines the amount of AP you have at the start of each turn as well as the order of which characters take their turns in. The combat is fairly fast paced similar to X-com enemy unknown, there is both cover and crouch mechanics too. The cover system is simplistic and being in cover gives you defensive bonuses. Crouching on the other hand improves your chance to hit as well as raising your chance to evade attacks.
Depending on the difficulty combat can become fairly challenging. Particularly later in the game when you meet tougher enemies and enemies with both unique mechanics and better weaponry. As you go through the game you can gain followers to your squad, these followers if you don't have the leadership skill can have a chance to lose control and they will do as they please in combat. Your weapons can also jam, usually at most inconvenient times, plus you will have to regularly reload your mags and watch your available ammo.
Overall the combat is solid, challenging and fun. It can throw you a few curve balls along the way too which is always good for keeping you on your toes. It's something that InXile had to get right and thankfully in my opinion they have executed it very well.
Wasteland 2 boasts a large number of quests to embark on. The great thing about the game is that you often have the freedom of choice in how to deal with the situations you encounter. Depending on who you have in your party and your skills, there are often multiple outcomes to any given scenario. An example of this is when I went to a graveyard and dug some graves, all was fine with me looting form the dead however upon reloading an earlier save I gained a different follower on the path and when I went to dig the graves my ally took offence to disturbing the dead and turn on my group. Things like this can happen all the time in the game and its great to see all the different possibilities there are. Not only does it ensure a good amount of re-playability but it also ensures that while two people can play the same game, different things will happen to each.
In conclusion wasteland 2 lives up to its namesake and not only provides a great post apocalyptic rpg experience but it provides a memorable one too. You will spend hours laughing at the video game culture references throughout the game as well as enjoying the well written characters. One thing I love is that the game doesn't hold your hand and lets you solve problems as you see fit, if there’s a wall in your way you could use the brute force skill or just throw a grenade, the choice is yours but the game won't tell you to do either, its up to you to come up with a solution if at all. The games story is strong and with its multiple choice system, there’s plenty to see and do. It's a solid title from InXile and something that you certainly felt after having such a successful crowd funding campaign, one that had to get right. While its release date has been pushed back several times, in all it seems it was worth it and Brain Fargo and the team have created a fitting sequel. While it does have its occasional issues and minor bugs, its a game that I would highly recommend adding to your collection. Whether your an avid RPG player or not, the majority of gamers will find hours worth of enjoyment in Wasteland 2.

Another Falcom title and another great localisation from XSEED. These guys are on a roll with me , ever since I have played Trails in The Sky FC like 5 years ish ago , I have been nothing but satisfied with these games. And for a falcom fan such as me this game was kind of a fanservice considering the stuff this game takes from the other ones in terms of mechanics.
Gameplay:
You like Ys , Gurumin or Brave Fencer Musashi (that one is a square title) , then you will like the gameplay here. Its fast , combo based and really fun. Also really convinient just like the other falcom titles. You can easily swtich between your weapons whenever , levelling up is not grinding but by using food items and you can upgrade your food items by trading them meaning yeah you can grind or just use healing items when you need to meaning you will level up according to your skill and the duo mechanic is very unique and fun. I love comboing my enemies by switching between these characters. Both of their attacks bring something to the table. Also just like Ys you can teleport to the save points meaning you can use that as a short cut too.
Presentation:
While yes this is an old game I personally think that it has aged rather well. Falcom really knows how to use its budget to make games look good and because of their uniqe art styles the games usually end up aging well.
The music......ahem ......COME ON!!! ITS FALCOM WE ARE TALKING ABOUT HERE!!! .......It is great....
The voice acting is also pretty good too. Infact some of the characters I just love seeing purely because of their voices. It only has english dub though (legal reasons) but there are work arounds for that stuff if you are a "ONLY JAPANESE!!!" sort of guy.
The characters and NPCs are all lovable people and while its no trails in the sky , this game has A LOT of dialogue especially considering what type of gameplay is being used here.
Unlockables:
Holly......like this is one area this game definitely beats Ys games over , there are A TON of stuff to do in this game. Like seriously. I am still not done yet and I am a fairly competent gamer myself when it comes to Falcom games.

So overall I can easily recommend this game if you are looking for a fun and cute action rpg and if you are already a falcom fan you have probably already bought the game.
Thank you XSEED for bringing this game over and thank you Falcom for making it. You guys are the best!

It's not difficult to tell that I'm a Falcom fanboy.  Ever since I played Ys III and Faxanadu decades ago, and renewed when I saw the Ys II Eternal trailer over 15 years ago, I've been helplessly in love with the games this company makes.  I've imported several of their games over the years, but not being able to read Japanese has limited my enjoyment of them.
I imported Zwei II+ 7 years ago and loved the game.  The gameplay, the music, the charm, the weird workout guy, it was the perfect package.  But I had no freaking clue what they were saying!  It was a very straightforward game so I was able to finish it and complete everything, but I was always sad I couldn't enjoy it as much as I should.
Thank goodness for XSEED feeding my inner fanboy, as I can finally enjoy Zwei II the way I was supposed to the first time!  Everything that made the game wonderful is still there, but being able to relate to the quirky characters and the story has made it so much more enjoyable.  It was funny to find out that the little trio of fairies are bickering about where to open a tailoring shop! :D
There are some minor issues that are worth mentioning.  The font isn't perfect, the bottom part of some letters will get cut off.  It doesn't impact the game, but it is a minor annoyance factor (that will hopefully be patched out in the future).  Additionally the framerate performance is not up to what I would expect from a game that released almost a decade ago.  I can play games with complicated 3D graphics like Destiny 2 at relatively high settings, but I have to turn down shadows in this to achieve 30 FPS.  This game wasn't written native to DX9 so it may just be growing pains preventing it from achieving optimal performance.
I love Zwei, and I'm very happy XSEED brought it to English speaking audiences.  The game is amazing, and it's an easy recommendation to make!

This review contains no spoilers!!!
This game gets criticized heavily on the dialogue. Having the teens say stuff like "cray" "Shaka bruh" "wowzers" which is pretty cringy indeed. I'm fresh out of high school and have found myself saying these thins only years ago and laugh at how well they captured the insecurity with the language that the teenagers use through out the story. It gives it a second hand embarrassment kind of feel, because you can relate to it.
The character models sometimes lack emotion, but the art is beautiful. There's an aesthetic the game has with the characters and background. They don't try to have cutting edge graphics but it works cohesively with the story. You play as a photographer and often can wonder off a little and feed the squirrels to get a picture of them up close. Often showing you scenes from the eyes of the photographer and not just what you make happens.
I absolutely love choice matters games. But this one takes the cake for me. Absolutely NO quick time events!! You can sit there and ponder about every outcome because it doesn't rush you to make a rash decision. It's one of my favorite parts of the game.
I've played through this game several times to see how the outcomes play through. Even looking or not looking threw a single cabinet can change your story a lot.
Finally, one of my favorite things about this game is that because it's a small company it's not afraid to have risky material. This game deals with depression, self doubt, insecurities, dealing with loss and suicide. It's LGBT friendly(even a possible romance!!) and has characters dealing with rough stuff. Even the biggest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in the game have a story. The side characters end up feeling real with there tales of metal illness and just all in all being confused. I've laughed and cried along with this game more times than I can count.
All in all, this is my all time favorite game and I recommend it to anyone who is a casual player to an adventure player and anything in between.

This little joy is direct from Dennaton Games- if you haven't heard of them, you will soon!
Hotline Miami is "A Clockwork Orange" set to the tune of 80's disco amongst flashing neon lights, as the player dispatches Russian mobsters with considerable prejudice. This ultraviolent game is challenging, make no mistake! The player will probably die. A lot. But, as with Arma Cold War Assault, that only makes the reward THAT much sweeter, and the victory THAT much tastier. It takes some work, but the results are well worth it. The game's exploration of the "protagonist's" obvious mental instability only makes the player feel like they are traversing the Congo River in Conrad's Heart of Darkness. Each progression in the game thrusts the main character deeper into the throes of insanity, until the player can no longer distinguish reality from a bad dream. The story is top notch, and the 80's-inspired soundtrack is what drives this game's ferociously intense pace. This game would get a 9.9 (any game rated a 9.9 and above is an instant classic in my book), but the options to not only uncover the game's secrets via another character, but to actually PLAY that character (a slice of awesome, with an amazing crib and quicker combat style- he's the true protagonist in MY book) means that it fully deserves the 10/10 rating that I give it.
Pat on the back to Dennaton for this masterpiece.

No, really. If you are like most folks on Steam, you have looked at the discussions for Shuffle, and you have seen the mixed review sign. People get all bent out of shape for this VN not being the Essence + version or this not being the old MangaGamer version.
First of all, I can assure you that this otaku and long-time fan of anything anime has played many, many visual novels. Shuffle is one of the very best. The way the choices made in the game lead to the different waifus is not necessarily logical, but trust me when I say it makes more sense than the sequels (Tick! Tack! and Really? Really?!). The real value here is in the character development and excellent voice acting. The story is actually light-hearted and fun. And the hero is a genuinely likeable guy instead of someone that might not actually deserve a girlfriend.
Second of all, since I am a natural-born citizen of the United States, I can say that I am an American. (And unlike a certain ex-president of the United States, there is no question about the authenticity of my birth certificate.) Therefore, I understand this  whole matter of censorship and why people hate it. I have played MORE than my share of eroge downloaded from sites like MangaGamer and J-List. And while I do heartily recommend that people give those sites business, I must say that Shuffle! does not need erotic content to be a VERY good VN. It has unexpected plot twists, great dialogue, and even seperate references to Mephistopheles and the Vestibule of Hell. (Those are from Dante's Inferno...this story is about gods and demons living on Earth, after all...even if the Japanese version of Kami-san is a bit different from the traditional Judeo-Christian version.)
Thirdly, the "On The Stage" (Steam) version of Shuffle features two VERY good endings to the game: Mayumi and Kareha-sempai. They are worth experiencing. This whole VN is worth experiencing...but since I played the MangaGamer version of this VN over 40 hours, I was quite happy to experience Kareha's and Mayumi's endings.
Experience the roller coaster of emotions that is Shuffle! You are in for a treat.
Edit: I did actually play the Asa-senpai route. It was great. It kept the spirit of the original VN without the explicit violence of the original version.

*** 1200 hours of gameplay ***
This game is fantastic. Whether you want to build planes and ignore the spaceflight part or mod the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the game, or go full hardcore and fly to Eeloo and back with no quicksaves, this game is for you.
The game has 3 modes: Sandbox, Science, and Career.
Sandbox: Self-explanatory. Infinite money and all parts are unlocked.
Science: Start out with basic parts and gain more science points by doing experiments on missions.
Career: Same as science mode, but funds and reputation are now something to consider.
The game features very realistic orbital mechanics; all bodies except for planets, moons and the sun follow n-body simulations. There is no real story, the goal is to do whatever the hell you want. I've erased the planet a few times through exploitation, so there's plenty to do.

-helps you understand physics and math
-little green men to use as test subjects

-easter eggs and anomalies all over every single planet
-get 1000 science points for a surface sample of a gas giant
-physics abuse
Cons:

Absolutely recommend, hours of fun and laughs to be had. Be warned though, its hard to understand at first.

My final score for Alan Wake is 9/10.
Alan Wake is an amazing game that is definitely worth your time and money.
MY FULL REVIEW OF ALAN WAKE:
Alan Wake is one of those games that has slipped under my radar, until about a week ago when I started playing it. The game is a psychological thriller, with some action and survival horror elements as well. It is a breath of fresh air from all those action-packed games I've played recently, and playing it feels really good, because it's simply a great game.
Set in a fictional town called Bright Falls, the game tell an engaging story about Alan Wake, a successful novel writer who has not been able to write anything for two years. Alan goes on vacation with his wife, Alice, to clear his mind. They find a nice and quiet place called Bright Falls. On the way there, Alan has a nightmare about him being chased by a dark figure, and he finds out that this dark figure is a character from one of his books. After they arrive at Bright Falls, things go wrong when Alice gets kidnapped by dark forces, and Alan has to find her, while being chased by a mysterious force called the Darkness.
What the game does best with the story is confusing the player, so that sometimes it's difficult to tell if all that's happening is real or just a nightmare Alan's having. Over the course of the game you will also find manuscripts that Alan supposedly wrote but can't remember writing them. You may find manuscripts that reveal something that hasn't happened yet in the game, but will happen soon, which is sometimes terrifying to know that pretty soon you are going to be facing what you read about in the manuscript.
Overall, the story is excellent and the writing is top notch. It actually feels like you're playing a great psychological thriller book, it keeps you invested in it, it's filled with twists, mysteries and the characters are interesting.
The story is divided into 6 episodes, and it's kind of like a TV show. Each episode is about 2 hours long, which makes for a total of 11-12 hours for the whole game, give or take.
Alan Wake has a unique combat system, where the player has to use the flashlight on creatures called Taken, which are weak to light, in order to destroy the Darkness shield that surrounds them, and then shoot them to finish them off. The light not only destroys the Darkness shield, but it also stuns enemies, and they back off when you point the light on them.
What's truly remarkable about the gameplay, is that it does a great job of keeping you tense, making you feel like you're in a survival horror game where every shot counts, which is not entirely true in this game, but you do have to be wary with your shots, because in some cases, you can find yourself being surrounded by 5 enemies having only 10 bullets left in your revolver, and it’s a pretty long way until the next ammo supply. Also, the flashlight needs batteries, so you are going to need batteries if you want to proceed further. Other tools that you can find in the game are flares, which keep enemies away for a short period of time, the flare gun and flash grenades which are really satisfying to use because they can vanish multiple enemies in one use. Enemies in the game don't feel too overpowered or underpowered; however, I wish that there would be more variety of enemies. Fighting the Taken just feels too repetitive, because the game throws a group of Taken at you every few minutes, and every encounter is always the same thing.
Another great mechanic is the dodging. When timing the dodge correctly, the game will trigger a Cinematic Dodge, which is a slow motion, bullet-time like dodge. It's pretty neat.
There are also collectibles and secrets scattered around the game for you to find, from hidden chests to coffee thermoses.  That's bound to make people who like achievements, like me, busy while playing.
One of the most important aspects in Alan Wake is the visuals, the atmosphere during the night is astonishing, with an incredible and well-designed forest and the fog covering it. It’s overwhelming. Lighting effects are one of the best I've ever seen in any video game ever, especially the flare lights, it's just too beautiful. That's not a surprise though, considering the game focuses on light as the main weapon, and the idea that light destroys the darkness.
The graphics are great, and they looked really good on my PC.
A fantastic soundtrack plays throughout the game, it's tense and creepy, and it's a soundtrack that should be put in a horror movie, or a TV series, that's why it fits perfectly into the setting of the game and the atmosphere. When an enemy encounter is imminent, the music changes into a more intense music, making you feel like you're fighting for your life, which you are, technically speaking.
Like I mentioned before, the game is amazing.
The story is fantastic, although it may be a bit confusing, visuals and gameplay are excellent, and the soundtrack is great as well.

When TellTale announced a Lego Avengers game inspired from the Lego Marvel game, you'd be foolish to not be excited. Following the media over the coming months was exciting to see all the new and returning characters. Myself and the fan-base had huge expectations for this title and in general they have succeeded!
The gameplay is vastly improved from previous titles including the previous Marvel title, and like many id shooters are fantastic to play this game shares that emotional bond with the player. It feels amazing to be able to play as these characters in third person and the story is incredibly immersive. My favourite parts of this title were in fact the fast pace action sequences leading towards the later parts of each chapter of the story.
On that note, the game has drawbacks which simply didn't exist in the original Marvel Lego game. Everybody was expecting the game's maps to be at least as big as the previous Marvel title. It featured a massive map with a lot to do, and anybody with a love of the franchise felt obligated to explore, collect and keep going back. I never got that vibe here as the maps size felt limited and the content feels limited in that I don't have a lot of interest in coming back.
Exclusive platform-based content has put a damper in the mix where I don't feel the publishers are treating all of it's customers as equal. There is still an ongoing issue that the Lego Hobbit game only features two of three parts - this game and future Star Wars titles run that same risk. It's a great idea, but if it cannot be guarenteed I can't put my heart into it. This is leading to the fact we can expect at least double of the content that there already is to come in the future - so I have no obligation to complain about the length, price or quantity of content on the whole (yet).
On the whole it's a fantastic game, but it comes with many areas which are fraught with a risk of disappointment, and many of this games anticipations transpired from the successes of their previous Marvel title.

The pickaxe left. Pickaxe flew away.

Days have passed and I've been so alone, but a glimmer of light appeared out of nowhere.
It was a red umbrella, so beautifully lush and shiny.
It became my new best friend.
I am happy, once again.

On the inExile forum there is the discussion how to rate the game 1-10.
I give it a plain 9/10.
Is it looking like a modern game is expected to look. No. But the graphics transport the atmosphere in a way modern engines lack. In fact it´s not the graphics that lack, but the story and sometimes the gameplay.
And that´s because it only gets a 9 - there is room for improvement, the combat system is well known from Fallout, the first parts, though it differs. I do miss some more tactical options, like delayed ambush or the ability to protect a weaker char. On the other hand it leaves you room for unorthodox methods of defeating an enemy.
Still Jagged Alliance had the best combat system ever.
So why give it a 9?
It transports the original feeling, many of you might not have experienced, so well, i hardly can get myself away from it, even if i should - get some sleep, just take a break or make something to eat that takes more than 5 mins of preparation.
Back when the orignal Wasteland was released i did not play RPGs, nor was my english (german here) any good.
And i have to say that Wasteland and an english-german dictionary was quite advancing my knowledge, shortly after  i began reading english books.
In Wasteland 1 there were no fancy 3d graphics, no sound and surely no voice acting. If you have the digital deluxe edition, try the old one, if you haven´t experienced the DOS era, you might think, how the hell anybody could play such a game.
Well, it was like a good book. You had to image the places you visit, only having (great) text based descriptions to fan your fantasy.
I can still picture the inside of Cochise base.
And there is one thing W2 does a lot better - it gives you more directions. W1 was pretty much open world, leaving one often with no clue what to do next, except from mentioning a city somehow. I do remember i had no idea how to get the visa card for the guy in... Needles, Quartz? Well he eats them, but that i needed it and how to get it....
In W2 you are pointed more directly in the right direction, but still you have to figure out how to solve things. I miss that a lot in modern games - as long as you can shoot stuff, you win. Quite boring.
The storytelling is great, if you take your time to read all the stuff. READ? Yes you have to read a lot and it is rewarding, though some areas have a bit too many people telling pretty much the same about the situation. Nevertheless, Wasteland 2  is a more than worthy and greatly rewarding game, that lives it´s orginial strengths inside a modern shell.
Modern? But you sais the graphics... Yep, i did.
Again, it does not take a 3d engine that requires 5 Nvidia Titans in SLI Mode to make a great game.
And there´s the matter of time a game takes. Okay a good deal is reading, but i consider those modern games, i play through in 16 hrs. straigt still entertaining - but way to short, even if they look fantastic, but i often find myself that i don´t value the work the company put into it, just because the game ruhes me by it. W2 slows you down. And that is a good thing.
I spend DAYS with the original Wasteland. I have spend DAYS with the Early Access already and thats just 50% of the game, though i replayed a bit, tested other options.
Where other games need a DLC after those 16 hrs gameplay you paid for, that will enterain you for 2 hrs at most, this game just sucks up your time and you want to do it again, just a different way next time, or just doing it better the next time.
Do i recommend it? Though i cannot judge the other half, if you like a great story, with more than adequate presentation, tactical combat and some serious dark humor, i don´t think you can go past Wasteland 2 - even if it´s not a 9 for you.

Rather than go through what many other people and websites are, I am only going to say I love this game.  It is both a wonderful reminder of some of the best RPG games from the past while also adding some freshness to the Genre.
If you are into RPG games with turn based tactical combat, I highly recommend this game.

For anyone looking to buy the game, I'll suggest to wait for a price drop. I bought the game for 54 usd dollar, but I don't think It deserves that much.
Yes the game was initially locked at 30 fps, but aside from that, the game runs smoothly on my PC. However, the graphics in general will not blow you away.
I'll update the list of pros and cons as I progress in the game:
Pros:
1-Story driven, focuses on characters.
2-The driving in the game is fun and responsive
3-The songs on the radio stations are great
4-Combat, shooting and sneaking around is fun.
5-Unlike other users I didn't face any type of crashes, the game runs smoothly.
6-Completing the optional missions are rewarding.
7-Multiple Endings.
8-And yeah, Donovan is ♥♥♥♥ing awesome.
Cons:
1-The enemy AI is kinda dumb, even on hard difficulty, including running away from the police. However, if you are spotted, every enemy with a shotgun can reach yout with their bullets like a sniper.
2-Three radio stations only.
3-Many of the the smaller missions, the ones that are required to pressure a racket leader to come out, are extremely repetitve. Combine that with the long storyline, and the game gets boring quickly.
4-Average graphics even on high settings. It's abvious that the game is not optimized for PC.
5-Some animations are outright missing, for example if the a car hit the main character, there is no animation of falling or getting hurt, your health will go down, and that's it.
6-The checkpoint system needs improvement.
7-No bikes/bicycles.
8- Even though the game didn't crash on me once, the game is filled with bugs that ruin the overall experience.

Stop me if this sounds familiar:
A young red-haired adventurer crash-lands on a mysterious island where he quickly gets roped up into helping a pretty girl recover elemental-themed McGuffins from maze-like dungeons filled with assorted monsters, baddies, puzzles and skulking villains, located across the island. Combat occurs in real-time, with the red hero jumping and slashing and collecting various bits and bobs that explode out of monsters' bodies when they die. You can switch at any time to another character, who wields a different weapon, with different enemies being more or less vulnerable to different attacks.
It's pretty much Ys, ya' see?
Zwei: The Ilvard Insurrection differentiates itself mostly with how seamless the combat is--even though your playing as two different characters, mechanically it only ever *feels* like one (and they share the same health pool and stats)--and through its innovative, rather transformative leveling system.
To level up in Zwei (actually Zwei II; don't ask) you need experience, but you can only earn experience by eating food (which heals you). If you don't eat, you don't grow stronger. Furthermore, once you have a stack of 10 food items, you can exchange them for 1 food item of the next tier-up. So, for example, say you have 10 Red Apples that will give you +5 experience each. If you eat them one-at-a-time, that's 50 experience. But you can exchange them for 1 Superior Green Apple that gives 100 experience. This creates an interesting dynamic where the more skilled you are at the game, but more experience you'll be able to accumulate, but consuming items for experience means having fewer healing items at hand, thus encouraging more skilled play.
It's a really effective system that gives the player a lot of freedom with how difficult combat is, and the diminishing experience rewards imbue many of the harder fights (the bosses) with a great deal of tension.
Beyond that, Zwei is pretty much exactly as good of a game as you'd expect from Falcom, with as good of a localization as you'd expect from XSEED. That is to say it is a very good game with a very good localization (though the default sound mixing leaves a bit to be desired--you'll probably want to turn the BGM waaaaay down before you start). Tonally Zwei is a bit lighter than you might expect--like the Disgaea games, this is a story walking a tightrope between serious and silly, and for the most part it succeeds brilliantly. The music is catchy and memorable, the characters are all quirky and unique (w/ lots of funny dialog), and much like the classic Trails series, every NPC in the game gets new dialog after every major story beat that eventually coaelesce into these fun little miniature character-arcs and stories for those who are willing to seek them out.

Ill start off by saying that i havnt played any of the other versions of this game (so cant comment on them)and that i got this with a random coupon and using steam cash for selling a card from a game I got for free (in short I got it for free) after coming home from the pub, so my expectations weren't that high.
This is a multi path branching choice based VN following some pretty standard VN norms of the protagonist being put into a situation where he has a chance at a number of 'good looking gals'.
+
OK skeleton for the story to hang from
ok art for the time of release
good number of branches
-
UI is poor (shows this versions console roots)
the story has obviously been butchered to fit into 'all ages' and not rewritten with any skill.
There are worse VN's out there but I wouldn’t get this unless it was on a 50% (or greater) sale as this is a lazy attempt to try and cash in on the 'cute' market from the publisher. The story has far to many fade to black/white screens and its obvious where huge chunks of the original story has been hacked out just to make it 'all ages' (probably from when in went over to the consoles). There is no skip forward ability which on a multi path vn means you are stuck clicking through long stretches of repeated material. The protagonist is actually more believable than most you’ll find in other VN's and the girls paths are all fairly coherent (if you ignore the gaps in the story) and the supporting characters are good if a little over the top.
Its a bit of a shame as I imagine this would have been a very good VN if its 'all ages' conversion had been handled with any skill or tact and if they had but some very basic functionality into the UI

This little joy is direct from Dennaton Games- if you haven't heard of them, you will soon!
Hotline Miami is "A Clockwork Orange" set to the tune of 80's disco amongst flashing neon lights, as the player dispatches Russian mobsters with considerable prejudice. This ultraviolent game is challenging, make no mistake! The player will probably die. A lot. But, as with Arma Cold War Assault, that only makes the reward THAT much sweeter, and the victory THAT much tastier. It takes some work, but the results are well worth it. The game's exploration of the "protagonist's" obvious mental instability only makes the player feel like they are traversing the Congo River in Conrad's Heart of Darkness. Each progression in the game thrusts the main character deeper into the throes of insanity, until the player can no longer distinguish reality from a bad dream. The story is top notch, and the 80's-inspired soundtrack is what drives this game's ferociously intense pace. This game would get a 9.9 (any game rated a 9.9 and above is an instant classic in my book), but the options to not only uncover the game's secrets via another character, but to actually PLAY that character (a slice of awesome, with an amazing crib and quicker combat style- he's the true protagonist in MY book) means that it fully deserves the 10/10 rating that I give it.
Pat on the back to Dennaton for this masterpiece.

1. Open Files.
2. Go to the drive where you installed your KSP.
3. Go to Program files (x64 or whatever)
4. Go to "steam"
5. Go to "steamapps"
6. Go to "common"
7. Go to "Kerbal Space Program"
8. Open GameData
9. Get the mod file
10. Put it in the GameData file
11. Play KSP

Hotline Miami pays a lot of homage to the 1980s in terms of gameplay as well as graphics and the music, which both restricts aspects of the game, but also provides a certain depth to it that one would not begin to grasp and appreciate at first glance. The controls are very basic given the nature of the game, but provide a myriad ways of stratagey. It's ultra-violence is a big selling point as there is no shortage of heads to bash, eyes to push into sockets, or limbs and bodies to dismember. The levels are repetitive and the enemies predictable but it's admissible and somewhat applauded given the sheer nostalgic feel to the game. The music is the highlight, it's one of the best soundtracks to any game I've ever played. The gameplay is fast paced and addictive, with a fair share of frustrating moments that add to the satisfaction upon completion, which also adds to replay value.
Overall, though it's not a lengthly game, this is not only a stand-out top-down action shooter but one of the most unique and enjoyable gaming experiences I've ever had.

Another one of those games that I wish steams' review system had a grey "neutral" rating for, because "It's complicated" doesn't even begin to discribe how I feel about this release of shuffle. While I am happy to see the day Shuffle is on steam.... god so many issues.
This is essentually the Playstation 2 all ages version of shuffle "On the Stage" which removed all adult content and added two additional routes (Mayumi and Kareha) as a reason for anyone who owned or played the original to have a reason to buy it.
I, like many it seems from what I've read in the other reviews, bought this for those additional routes as its the first time we've had them in offical english (I am specifically a Mayumi fan) and while I am semi satisfied with what I got. This really is a disappointing and inferior game to what we could and should be getting at this point.
I am not going to sugarcoat it even as a fan of the series. Shuffle is old, and has a limited appeal to people, yet they are pulling these blundered moves lets examine things:
1) The steam version being non-adult.
While this isn't a huge surprise, it is a little disappointing in an era where there are ways to provide adult content and not step on people's toes (taking examples of Nekopara, Huniepop, etc) where a one step disconnection from steam allows people to get their adult content and still sell an all ages product which allows neither market to be alienated. It really is getting to a point where there is no acceptable excuse for this and either YumeHeaven or Navel is too lazy to look into these avenues, or does not want to give us the adult content, either one is not something I agree with.
2) Giving "On the Stage" instead of "Essence+"
The first issue about adult content is annoying but like in the PS2 era from which On the Stage originated, they gave two new routes to compensate it. Essence+ is a shuffle release that came later that also added adult content to said routes. Lets once again not sugar coat things; Shuffle is a game that's 12 years old, Essence+ is 7 years old. Its not a stretch to believe at the very least if they are going to deny people adult content, to atleast give us Essence+'s level of routes and options. So why give us every single mediocre nickel and dime version in between?
These companies seem to live in a world where they think people do not research products and are unaware that stuff like Essence+ has existed for many years. Which is frankly insulting if you think we're that stupid, it should have been the definitive release of shuffle cause its likely the only one steam might ever see.
3) Weird localization choices.
I am not going to go too heavy into this cause its barely a footnote for me, but it has annoyed some people so its worth atleast touching upon. The basic idea of this is the mangagamer script was very well done and established a certain expectation to what things would be called, the YumeHeaven scripts make some completely uneccessary and often bizzare changes. While I can personally survive these changes, its perfectly logical to why some people are very upset.
In the end Navel/YumeHeaven you should seriously step up your game because while this sold to people, it seriously was weaksauce and many wont be so eager to jump on the next thing you sell.

Fun, but more crashes than a destruction derby, and more unstable than a 2 legged giraffe.
The game improves on the original with it's expanded combat, however I'm pretty sure the graphics aren't as good as the original game, and the crashes I've experienced are the worst from ANY game I've played on any system, and I've been gaming actively almost every day since about 1986.
My system is an i7 4790k, 16GB RAM and a pair of Nvidia Titan X GPU's.  Everything is watercooled, on Win10 and my system is very stable.  If games crash on me, I know it's either Windows playing up, or the game itself.  All my drivers are up to date.
I run the game at 4k like most of my other titles.  I get full GPU scaling from both cards and get around 60FPS and the gameplay is fluid at max settings and HDR enabled to my 4k HDR LG OLED C6V.
I think so far this game has crashed on me roughly 20 times, but it is probably more.  This includes a lot of bluescreen errors, or random system rebooting.  I also had one crash which gave a driver error, and one which gave a gpu timeout error.
After using DDU to remove my drivers and a fresh install of the updated driver, the crashes were less frequent, and went from every 10 minutes to every hour.  Using the recommended fix to set the render config to Borderless completely prevented the game from launching at all.
I can't recommend the game in it's current state at all, even though the combat, loot and skills are actually quite fun.  In fact I'm starting to wonder how Warner Bros. manage to stay in business with products in such bad shape, and their dubious track history on PC.

This is what Flappy Bird would have looked like if it was permanently fixed on death match with multi-players, the title was simplicity at its best while remaining a blast to play at parties.
The game play consist of two or more players controlling their characters with a single button press, while the duration of your press dictates the height of which you fly. Sounds simple? Well, did I mention that you also have to avoid spike traps, other players, along with the dreaded borders of doom?
It gets more hectic with the more players you have, which is a good thing, especially when you have friends over for a bout. Even if you are the type that’s forever alone, you can have an awesome battle between your left hand and right hand, in which my right hand always win.
Slight warning though if you’re planning on using a single keyboard. Unless you have a mechanical keyboard with some specialised drivers, it is not likely to register more than four key presses at the same time. So I would recommend a controller or two on the side to even out the players on each input device.
The DLC packs are not required in any way, but they do add more characters and hats, it won’t hurt to buy some if you happen to like the game and support the developer.

The story's protagonist is a writer who travels to a small mountain town called Bright Falls (ironically as 90% of the game is played at night) in an attempt to clear his head of writing. His wife decides that she doesn't want him to relax and so gets him a typewriter. Alan gets mad because he wants to relax on his vacation (for whatever reason) but he's interrupted by the lights going out in the house that is in the middle of a lake... bad planning... also his wife is afraid of the dark. The beginning of the story is when all the lights are still on and you are able to meet the townsfolk, however after only a few minutes of interaction it all falls apart and you don't get to see the town, or anyone except for your bumbling assitant (editor? I don't know but he wore a stupid jacket and never shot anyone and the game wouldn't let me kill him) and throughout I wanted to see the town as it was however the game makes you constantly hunt and scavenge for ammo for shotguns, pistols, rifles, flareguns etc. and fight off (even admitted by the game devs) endless waves of enemies which ruins the atmosphere. I think I would have been thoroughly frightened had the enemies not been so overwhelming in number, so that once you kill all the enemies on the screen and run 3-5 steps, another group crops up. And don't bother trying to conserve ammo, the game takes it all away from you whenever it gets the chance. Also the dialouge makes me cringe. The game had a chance to be beautiful and rich in story but overloads the player with darkness, stupid goals and inconveniences, ridiculous plot twists, and hordes of enemies. I recommend the game only because the story is still really good but becomes a chore if you play it too much and too often

POSTED: February 1, 2016
UPDATED: June 25, 2016
Lego Marvel's Avengers is a Lego action-adventure video game developed by TT Games and published by Warner Brothers, releasing on the PS4, PS3, PS Vita, 3DS, Wii U, Xbox One, Xbox 360, and for PC, releasing on Steam in January 2016.
After 100% completing the game, I'm able to base my review on literally everything the game has to offer, besides most of the new DLC.
The game's story takes place through various scenes in 6 of the MCU (Marvel Cinematic Universe) movies, such as; The Avengers, Captain America: The First Avenger, Iron Man 3, Thor: The Dark World, Captain America: Winter Soldier, and The Avengers: Age of Ultron, with the exception of future DLC that includes Ant-Man and possibly others. They currently have a deal with Sony for a time exclusive DLC featuring an Ant-Man story/characters and Civil War characters, which will release in a few months for all other platforms.
First thing's first, is this better than Lego Marvel Superheroes?
In my opinion, yes and no.
Based on the roster, I liked Superheroes better because it had all of my favorite characters and the more iconic characters all in one. So don't go into this expecting to see Deadpool, The Fantastic Four, or the X-Men, as this game focuses soley on the Avengers MCU and comic universe. If Marvel doesn't own the sole rights to put them in a movie, they won't be in this game. But they still have a great roster of over 190 different characters.
Gameplay wise, it is much better. Combat seems more fluid. There are now combat specials where you use your second character to take down enemies. They added super jumps to certain characters. Speedsters are really fun to play as. Quicksilver is easily one of my favorites to play as, with their new mechanics. The voice acting for most of the main cast is ripped straight from the movies to give it an authentic feeling. For the most part, it sounds good, but there are parts where it just doesn't sound right. The graphics actually look much better, in my opinion. All returning characters have been completely revamped with new movesets and animations. Tony Stark and his Iron suits also have a neat animation when switching characters, that makes it seem like you're inside his helmet, like in the movies. Unlike Marvel Superheroes, there are now several different hub areas you can explore. They include Tony Stark's beach house in Malibu, S.H.I.E.L.D. HQ, South Africa, Hawkeye's farm, Slovenia, Asgard, and the return of Manhattan.
I did run into a few bugs here and there that caused me to restart a level or two, but nothing game breaking. A few freezes and stutters here and there, especially when flying or jumping, but otherwise, smooth 60 FPS on high settings.
I was able to completely beat the game in about 30 hours. That includes collecting all the gold/red bricks, vehicles/characters, Stan's in peril, and minikits.
Overall, it's a great game for any Marvel fan. I grew up playing the Lego series, and I still enjoy them today at 21. If you're a fan of the movies, you'll definitely be a fan of this game, as TT has yet to disappoint. The retail price is $40 at the time of this review, but with all Lego games, they'll likely drop down to $7.50 during a sale within the next year. If you can't wait, I was able to pick it up for about $10 from a third-party key seller website whose logo is a penguin. *hint hint*
If you found this review helpful, please give it a thumbs up.

I'm fairly new to the whole Turned-based strategy game genre at which I only played Shadowrun Returns, XCOM, and Divinity: Original Sin and now Wasteland 2. So with my experience out of the way now I might as well get on with it!
Wasteland 2 has not been regretted at all for an early access purchase, as to where I will be spending a lot of my time playing this game when the game fully releases! I feel that a lot of gamers anymore lose interest into these games, because it's not action 24/7 but I would say that these games now have got my attention and this game has taken over my life so far!
Pros:
1.) The environment is very detailed where it doesn't look pixilated at all and from that shows the time it took the developers to give a great Post Apocalyptic experience.
2.) The variety of skills to master in at which can change a lot in the future of game play from Toaster Repair, to being a Kiss♥♥♥♥♥to survivors. These will keep you thinking on which will be best for each character and from that can alter what your character can do.
3.) Character creation is very generic as to any other RPG element, but there's nothing wrong with that at all! Create your own character and make him/her a minigun wielding badass! But if you're not comfortable with creating your own character (or squad), you have preloaded characters to choose from at which have their own specialties for you.
4.) The combat system in the game can be very tense and frustrating (in a good way)! Every combat you encounter has you looking for anyway to wipe out your enemies as fast as you can from breaking through their coverage, to flanking them with your sniper. Every battle is definitely tense from where a simple 80% or above chance to hit still will miss (most frustrating thing in the world!!!!).
Cons:
1.) A few minor glitches in the game which is common for a early access game, but some are still effective even though you reloaded the game before that glitch happened.
2.) For my perspective and for anyone else who isn't too familiar with Turned-based strategy games, I had to restart the game a couple times as to where I screwed up and once you screwed up, you might as well restart and fix your mistakes. It may not seem like a con for others, but to me it's kind of frustrating to be restarting this game just to get it right.
Verdict:
I highly recommend this game for when it comes out, or even if you would like to play it right before it comes out! As for anyone who is considering buying the game full price, I would say that you wouldn't be disappointed in this purchase and would be looking forward to more hours of this game!

I love this game. If you've enjoyed past Lego games, you should at least give this game a look. If you're a fan of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, you should at least give this game a look. If you're both a fan of Lego games and the MCU you are doing yourself a gross disservice if you don't play this game. It's fun, it's funny, and there is soooo much to do. At the time of this review, I've got just under 18 hours played and all I've done is the story mode which covers the movies Avengers 1 & 2, Captain America 2, Iron Man 3, and Thor 2. There are still a ton of vehicles to unlock, a ton of characters to unlock, countless side missions I haven't gotten to yet, and several open world hubs to play in (including a pretty large open world Manhattan).
The puzzles are simple, but enjoyable. The combat is simple and fun in the typical Lego style, but with character specific grabs and team up moves added in. I'm still discovering new team up moves and new things the characters can do with their powers. Guilty pleasure? Climbing buildings and super jumping around the Manhattan hub as the Hulk.
I never thought my favorite movie game would be a Lego game. I was wrong...and I'm totally OK with that.
Update: Just 100%'d the game, took me 45 hours to do everything...and I never do everything. Definitely a solid amount of engaging content.

Two years ago, I was presented with an exciting opportunity to contribute money to one of my favorite game developers so that they could make a game that they really wanted to make.
I became a fan of Double-Fine after I purchased Psychonauts when it came out. I didn’t know much about the game before I bought it, but it instantly became one of my favorite games of all time. Since then, I’ve been following Double-Fine closely, eating up most games that they produce. I’ve had amazing experiences with Brutal Legend, Costume Quest, Trenched (Iron Brigade), Stacking, but the time I spent with Broken Age is unlike any other gaming experience I’ve ever had.
It all started when I paid a measly $15 to become a backer to an adventure game that I admittedly had no real interest in playing. My previous experiences with adventure games were underwhelming as I seemed to have missed all the good ones (like all of the Lucas Arts ones). As part of the deal for my money, I would also receive a documentary series about development of the game. I thought that would be cool, and I was happy to help them with whatever I could afford at the time.
What I didn’t expect was such outstanding installments of episodes to grace my inbox in the months to come. Not being a superstitious person, I knew that video game development wasn’t really magic. But I had no idea how it happened, until now. As a recent hire as a quality assurance specialist, I’ve been both getting experience in the software production, and learning the intricacies of game development from the documentary. I’ve always wanted a job in the industry, but watching the documentary series by 2 Player Productions has only reaffirmed and reinvigorated my drive to get one.
I’ve heard stories about gamers becoming more involved with the characters and story with adventure games, but I thought I was incapable of that kind of imagination. What Double-Fine did was nothing short of memorization. Beautiful art, funny dialogue, excellent storyline, interesting characters, unique environments, outstanding music, and the list continues. Twice, my jaw was left wide open. At parts of the game that I saw in the documentary, I felt privileged to know some of the background to the production of it. Even Hipster Jack made it into the game!
The best part? This is only part 1! I get to look forward to more episodes, and another installment of one of my favorite gaming experiences in recent memory. So my obligatory rating for this game is 10/10, 2 thumbs up, 5 stars, I have nothing but praise. Go out and buy this game, buy all their other games, participate in Amnesia Fortnight (also a game changing amount of awesome), and long live Doble-Fine.

I'm not entirely sure how they're able to get away with selling this game alongside gameplay videos and screenshots that are in no way representative of the end product. It's not just the 30 FPS, the graphics are extremely MUDDY and low resolution. Turning certain graphical features OFF actually makes the graphics improve, which makes me wonder if this is the developers first time working with a PC after a career developing slot machines for the app store.
Gameplay so far is a mixed bag too, in trying to make a true open world game this time around, the missions and objectives have less flavour to them. The AI is very clunky and stilted and moves predictably meaning you're rarely in any real danger. I have enjoyed the driving physics so far, the muscle cars in particular drift in a satisfying way, and the in-car combat system works well. I'm hoping further patches will help improve this - not just FPS, but fixing the AA and increasing the texture resolution so that it matches the screen resolution.

EDIT - 15-10-2016:
The game story is VERY good IMO and it's crazy good seeing Vito Scaletta back, even if we don't get to play as him :)
The gameplay is usually fluid until you hit a bug or two (usually problematic physics, NPC animation and reflections), which, honestly, are still plentiful (even on the consoles). Despite the bugs the game is enjoyable and hits just the right boxes for me - hoarding (posters, points of interest, money, territory, etc), INSANE soundtrack (I'm a big sucker for 60s-70s music!), great story and Godfather-style territory control.
I can't stress it enough - the story is GREAT! The cinematics and the way the story is told are really something I've not seen in a while. Big props for that!
Graphically the game is a bit of a hit-and-miss at times as it looks great in some lighting conditions but can also change to something that looks f*cking HORRIBLE. The textures are also on the low-res side, not something I'd expect in a 2016 title, especially after GTA V.
The performance is...meh... No SLI support so I'm running at 1440p on a single GTX 1080 and the framerates dip to the 50s sometimes, but can also go up into the low 90s. But considering what GTA V looks like and what Mafia III looks like and how they both run on my system - Mafia III leaves a lot to be desired... But it works and it's still a better version than the console one xD
It took a short while for 2K/Hangar13 to launch a few patches here and there to fix some annoying issues, but even after the 30fps lock removal I was already quite happy, to be honest. The superb cutscenes and the story really help you forget and ignore the bugs here and there.
Shame about the messy launch, but the game is definitely worth getting!

Aerodynamics (Your rocket will explode if you don't care), Gravity, Fuel Makes Your Rocket Heavier And You Take More Rockets Then You Need More Fuel Then......(It's a real problem in rocket science.), Will Parachutes At A Certain Speed Will Rip, Prograde, Retroprograde, Normal, Anti-Normal, Radial, Radial Out, Maneuvers, Gravity Assists, Asteroids, Extreme Heat From Slamming The Atmosphere, Vaccum Of Space, Life Support, Your Rocket Might Explode Spontanously, Losing The Crew, Docking, Space Stations, Missing targets, Accidentental Destruction Of Your Ship By Accidentally Crashing Into A Random Asteroid, Space Junk, Space Debris, Accidentally Flying Into The Sun, Crashing Into A Gas Giant, Worrying About The Heat Of Venus, Crashing Into Saturn's Rings (of doom?), Accidental Detonation On A C4 Strapped To Your Space Ship, Glitchy Rockets, Faulty Satellites, Being Destroyed By Ailens, Moon Containmation, Fuel Depletion, You Lost Your Aerodynamic Wings And You Crashed, Your Engines Overheated And You Blew Yourself Up, blah, blah, blah......
If you don't want to deal with these trillion things, just mess with the settings. Note, if you accidentally screw a vital settings that is required to e.g. launch the game, you're done.
OR, add mods.
I added a bunch of mods, and they worked perfectly. Just expect some little "bugs".
Just in case you don't know how to download mods, read this.
1. Open Files.
2. Go to the drive where you installed your KSP.
3. Go to Program files (x64 or whatever)
4. Go to "steam"
5. Go to "steamapps"
6. Go to "common"
7. Go to "Kerbal Space Program"
8. Open GameData
9. Get the mod file
10. Put it in the GameData file
11. Play KSP

A hidden gem I discovered during the IndieXmas event on twitter hosted by IndieGamerChick along with several developers. Worst part about the game is something that doesn't directly impact on the gameplay, it's the achievements. A couple of them are simply extremely ridiculous and pretty much lock anyone from legitimately complete the game 100% but at the time of this review the developer has stated that he plans to dial down those achievements so they aren't that punishing (Or rather outright impossible).
Another annoying thing is the lack of a restart button for when you're trying to get the S ranks. Other than that is a very enjoyable experience.

While my review is a positive one for the game itself, I'm really on-the-fence about the pricing. Depending on how good you are at the game, you can beat it in a couple of hours or even faster. The levels rank you based on time and collectibles, and I was able to get the maximum rank for every level in approximately 2.5 hours (two-and-a-half). There are 36 levels total, and, ignoring deaths/retries and mistakes, every level can be completed in 20 to 40 seconds... Thus, I wouldn't say this game is long by any means.
If you get the game and it does not run, look into:
The game was unable to launch for me on Windows 10, 64-bit, and apparently it was an error about not having OpenAL installed. I found that above link and used the "Installer" (not the programming SDK/core one) which installed the plug-in quickly and then the game worked.
The developer said he is looking into fixing this issue.
I bought the game simply off of interest with the screenshots and trailer. I don't usually buy games this quickly but I figured I would give it a shot.
The game is definitely very fast-paced and really banks on you moving through the levels quickly. While you can move the character at your own pace, the levels always go in one direction and sometimes will require you to continuously move in order to make progress; otherwise, if you move too slow, you might get stuck or die.
There is an "Autorun" setting in the options which I actually
after a couple of levels. Essentially, from that point forward, the game became a trial of learning how to time jumps, rolls, attacks, and so on, just using 2 buttons.
Each level has enemies and obstacles in it, as well as coins and fruit to collect. The fruit are actually weapons you can throw to knock out certain enemies, though some of them are invincible to the fruit. You can only carry 5 fruit at a time, so if you use some, collecting more will add back to your little inventory. The coins, on the other hand, are used for nothing but points and ranking in the levels.
Each level will give you a rank upon completion, with S being the highest. In order to get the S rank, you must complete the level within a time limit, collect all of the coins, and have your 5 fruit inventory full when you finish the level. In order to complete the time limits, using the "Autorun" is essentially necessary. So many of the levels, even if they have very few obstacles and lots of open space, might still be very difficult for their time limit. For instance, there were many times where I'd finish a level at 29.9 seconds, and the time limit was 30.0 seconds. Even making a single tiny mistake in some levels will make it impossible to reach the time limit.
Note,
, that the time limits and ranking are unrelated to progress in the game, and only exist if you wish to add even more challenge to what you are doing.
In any case, the story of the game is really not much of a story. The guy (Miles) and his dog (Kilo) get knocked out of the sky, and some creepy guys steal parts of their plane. You run through different areas until you reach boss levels, which still run similarly to the normal levels, except that you have to attack at certain times in a specific way and cannot just throw fruit at the bosses.
The graphics and sound are as they seem in the screenshots and trailer: retro-style and chip tunes. There's variety in the level design and also multiple songs in the game, so it's not the same thing over and over.
All in all, the game is really a lot of fast-paced motion and timing. There is no exploration. All of the levels are linear and can be very quick if you are good at reacting quickly. Despite that, I enjoyed the game, though I'm still on-the-fence about the pricing for it. It could probably be a couple of bucks cheaper.

The short of this review is that the Steam release of Shuffle! is plagued by various design issues, and is an inferior version of the game to the original Mangagamer release. If you really enjoy Kareha and Mayumi, it might be worth picking it up. Other than that, there isn't a reason to get this one. Phsyical editions of the original Mangagamer Shuffle are still available on J-list, thankfully, so look to get one of those.
If you're looking for a more detailed breakdown, read on.
This version of Shuffle! is a port and translation of the PS2 All-Ages release called Shuffle! on the stage. The game has 2 new routes compared to the last English version. It's a completely new translation by YumeHaven following Navel terminating their partership with Mangagamer. You can't buy the 18+ edition of Shuffle! anymore. There's not a patch available or anything. This also isn't the best and most complete version of the game: Shuffle! Essence+ has 4 more routes than this version. It's been out for about 7 years now, so people seem a bit annoyed that we're getting this version instead of that one. Although I would've preferred Essence+ to be translated, I'm sure it just wasn't an option. Maybe if the game sells well, we could see Essence+ released stand alone or as a DLC for this game.
Apparently this version of Shuffle drastically changes the dramatic parts of the original to be more kid friendly. I would wager that it's not because of the western launch they did that though, it's probably just how the game was changed for it's PS2 release. For that reason, I'm going to suggest buying the Mangagamer version instead of the Steam version if possible. You wouldn't just be buying it for the H scenes, you would be buying it for the proper tension and drama.
One of the biggest problems with this game is it's missing features. Functions that you've probably come use to having are just up and missing with this game. The original Shuffle runs in an engine dedicated to Visual Novels, and it definitely shows. You have lots of options, the 'CTRL' key is the default skipping button, you can use your scroll wheel to view the text log, you can change the text speed from a turtle's pace to instant, the transitions are all smooth... Using your noggin, you can probably guess why I'm talking about all the things the original release of Shuffle can do. I mean, the title of this section is "Functional Issues", right? Everything I just mentioned is straight up missing in the steam release of Shuffle. Really.
You can't skip unread text, and the only way to skip text is through the spacebar button. It's also a toggle, which means there isn't a "push to skip" button. If you try to skip to a certain line in text you've already read, you're liable to end up going right past it because you untoggled the skip function too late. No problem, you might say. I'll just return to that line using the text log! Well... You can't. The original Shuffle release doesn't let you rollback the scene either, but this is a completely new version with a completely new engine. Why wasn't this implemented? Want to see the message history using the scroll wheel? Too bad, hope you like hitting the "H" key. Also, there isn't a way to hide the text box. Yep, you're stuck with it. Want to see the character art without the dialogue bothering you? The only option is to open the right click menu. Which dims the entire scene and draws a dull looking set of options in front of you, "Save", "Load", "Settings", "Save and Quit", and "Quit". The last two actually quit to the main menu, despite just being called "Quit". Let's talk about the "Settings" option though!
You only have four options for in game volume control and text speed.
As mentioned earlier, none of those four options for the text speed are "Instant". Well... That's pretty much it! Thankfully, the settings do allow you to manually turn character voices off and on. Oh, and it also has a kind of worthless resolution mode. At first glace, you might think it's useful. But it's not. All it does is allow you to choose whether you want to have the sky themed border art. If you set the game to one of the 4:3 options, like 800x600, then fullscreen it on a widescreen display, it'll scale properly and just have black borders instead. So, the resolution options do basically nothing unless you want to use it in windowed mode! Which is good, but if that's the case, why can't we just stretch the game window to the size we want? It's not like the border art is real proper art, it's just a texture laid out over the unused portions of the screen.
The one good thing I can say about this release is that it has controller support. Definite kudos for that, every Visual Novel release should have controller support. That one good thing does pretty much nothing to cover up the many, many issues this title has though.
This is one of those titles that don't use honorifics for whatever reason. You can hear the characters say them, but they aren't shown in translation. It's jarring. There's no reason to be afraid of honorifics with a game like Shuffle. The vast majority of the playerbase jumping into this title will know what all the honorifics mean. Things like miso soup get mentiioned in the game without a proper explanation, so it's just baffling. The problem is most exemplified in Kareha's route, where Tsubomi calls the main character "Rin Onii-san", but the game translates it as "Handsome". That's definitely wrong... Even those of us completely unfamiliar with Japanese know that much. "Big Bro Rin" doesn't sound natural in English at all, but it wouldn't be an issue to begin with if honorifics were used! It's made even more confusing by the fact that at different points in the game both Kareha and Asa are referred to with "-Senpai". For future translations done by YumeHaven, I hope this will change. Other than that, the translation is quite nice. It likes to shy away from Japanese onomatopoeia though. Another good example from Tsubomi is how her "Kyaa!"s are translated as "Eeek!"s. Both of these words just feel too different... It's a situation where keeping the original is better. It's not like "Kyaa!" means anything, it's just the noise she's making.

I'm afraid to try out the other routes because of this...
10 - 20 hours of gameplay depending on reading speed / degree of completion / usage of skip.
Traditional visual novel setup where you have 1 common route with choices that branches into different character routes.
Unlike Choose-your-own-adventure games, choices do not alter how the common route plays out aside from minor differences to maintain consistency.  This means that you'll end up seeing the same scenes and choices on subsequent playthroughs despite making a completely different first choice on the common route.
I should mention that certain choices will reveal hidden scenes where you may be given additional choices.  These hidden scenes are key to unlocking certain heroine routes.  As I said before though, during the common route your choices do not cause the plot to deviate, so when you find a hidden scene, it will return to the common route eventually.
The key to finding a route is by picking the right combination of choices.  Thankfully, for those choices where the end result isn't obvious, this novel does provide a clue after each important choice indicating which girl would end up the happiest.  Just gather up as many moments with her as you can.
This game allows you to set a 1920x1080 resolution, but it's sort of a cop out.  Unlike the title screen, the game itself has the traditional 4:3 aspect ratio of the original.  The rest of the space is filled in with a cloud backdrop on the left and right side of the screen.  Even though you don't get HD CG, I'm okay with this since you can fullscreen without getting distorted sprites on widescreen monitors.  In the MG version, I had to either play windowed or tamper with my graphics card settings to keep the game's 4:3 aspect ratio.
This visual novel isn't one of the recent ones, so you'll find that while it is voiced, you won't get the dynamic animation that you would find in NekoPara, Go Go Nippon, or Corona Blossom.
In a recent patch, the music volume has been dialed down so that it doesn't drown out the voices.  The voices still aren't as crisp and clear as I would like though.  I'm not sure if it's because it's a port or the VA's are using a low quality microphone, but it feels like the characters are speaking to you from the other end of the room.
You can use a gamepad to play.  That's nice!  Sorta, you can really only use it to advance and select choices.  But it allows you to sit farther away from the computer while playing.  Maybe even in a reclined pose.
A recent patch has greatly improved the playability of the game.  First, the skip key is the [Ctrl] button now.  This may seem weird on the english speaking market, but for those that are familiar with Japanese Light Novels, this is the standard skip key.
History can be accessed by scrolling up on your mouse wheel in addition to hitting the "H" key.
The UI overlay can be hidden with the space key.
The config screen of this PS2 port is limited compared to traditional PC VN's. While you do get the standard stuff, a lot of the quality of life options that you would normally get are missing. For instance, there is no option to skip read/unread messages when skipping. And there isn't an option to continue playing voice when mouse clicked to end text layout. Nor is there an option to lay out text instantly at fastest speed.
The songs in the sound gallery now loop so you can keep your hands off if you want to hear a song again.  Yay!
Japanese Voice.  English text, no honorifics.
Translation is okay.  English is fluent and typos are uncommon. I'm tempted to call Nerine's shortened-name, Rina, a typo though.
Most of the changes are generally to fit in the 2 new character routes.  It makes me happy to see Mayumi with more screen time.
Some scenes have been expanded and moved around. For instance, observer reactions play a bigger part; it helps with the immersion because now we get glimpses of how the bystanders are reacting.  Some of them are even voiced with choice lines like "she's like a doll!".   It's not just the bystanders, the main characters have more moments too.
Certain scenes have been removed like that one with the crazy KKKaede fan and its followup.  The "bodyguards" are given a brief mention in the text, but without the acting you aren't aware of their true danger...
I kinda prefer how the original laid out the routes.
In this version of the game, the common route sort of blends into the heroine routes.  While you will unmistakably enter a heroine route, common route events will still occur inside of that route.
In the original, this blending didn't happen, once you were on the heroine route the story completely changed.
The reason why this even bothers me is because there is an event with Kareha that's basically bugged. This common route event will still happen even when you are on a heroine's route, and if you pick the "right" choice, you will find yourself forced out of that heroine's route and into Kareha's.
(6/10)
- Those that haven't played the game are going to wonder what's so great about it as the serious moments have been turned into bad comedy.
- Those that have played the MG version will be disgusted at the 4kids quality, it's-not-blood-it's-ketchup, censoring ruining the message.  For the Mayumi and Kareha fans, still checking the Mayumi and Kareha routes to see if they're worth playing, but I wouldn't buy this to collect it.
- With the new patch, in addition to the thoughtfulness of the screen resolution and gamepad input, the game has become comfortable to play.
